docs.title: CraftingBlueprints Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for CraftingBlueprints, an enterprise-grade Paper/Purpur plugin designed to transform recipe progression, economy balance, and custom crafting across modern Minecraft networks.

docs.title: What is CraftingBlueprints?
docs.text:
By default, Minecraft allows players to craft any unlocked recipe automatically. CraftingBlueprints introduces a true schematic progression system: players must discover, purchase, or earn physical or virtual Blueprints to craft specific weapons, armor, tools, or custom items.

Whether you operate a Survival SMP looking to gate Netherite gear, an MMORPG server with limited-use ancient forge scrolls, or a Skyblock network with tiered crafting licenses, CraftingBlueprints gives you absolute control over your server's crafting meta.

docs.title: Why Choose CraftingBlueprints?
docs.text:
• Stunning In-Game Map Schematics: Renders photorealistic technical blueprints directly onto standard 128x128 Minecraft maps (Material.FILLED_MAP) with 25 pre-calibrated background textures (magma, astral, slate, carbon weave), banknote-grade Guilloché borders, procedural item outlines, and rarity styling.
  • Selective Whitelist Mode: Don't want to lock every single recipe? Restrict only specific items (such as Netherite equipment, potions, or Beacons) while leaving basic wood, stone, iron, and farming tools completely natural and free.
  • Minecraft 1.21 Crafter Protection: Prevents redstone auto-crafters from bypassing your blueprint economy. Automated Crafter blocks that attempt to produce locked recipes are automatically intercepted and blocked cleanly.
  • Instant Multi-Server Synchronization: Supports both standalone embedded SQLite and high-performance MySQL with real-time heartbeat sync signals for BungeeCord and Velocity networks.
  • Declarative YAML & Hot-Reloading: Create hundreds of recipes cleanly using reusable templates (mixins), live file watching, and dry-run syntax validation (/cb validate).
  • Custom Items SPI Interoperability: Seamless out-of-the-box integration with ItemsAdder, Oraxen, Nexo, MMOItems, EcoItems, MythicMobs, and CustomModelData.

docs.title: Declarative YAML Blueprint Authoring
docs.text: All blueprints in CraftingBlueprints are authored declaratively in YAML files placed inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/. The plugin recursively scans this directory and all nested subdirectories (e.g. weapons/, armor/, potions/) in deterministic alphabetical order.

docs.title: Authoritative JSON Schema & IDE IntelliSense
docs.text:
To eliminate syntax errors, typo-induced bugs, and cognitive overload, CraftingBlueprints provides an authoritative JSON Schema (blueprint.schema.json).

To enable real-time autocompletion, field descriptions, and instant error highlighting in Visual Studio Code or IntelliJ IDEA, add this directive as the very first line of any blueprint YAML file:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json

docs.title: Anatomy of a Production Blueprint
docs.text:
Below is an exhaustive, production-ready blueprint configuration demonstrating every canonical property and sub-block:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  ancient_netherite_axe:
    # 1. Target Recipe to Unlock (Material, Custom Item, Potion, or Enchantment)
    blueprint: NETHERITE_AXE
    name: "<gradient:#FF5555:#FFAA00><bold>Ancient Netherite Battleaxe</bold></gradient>"

    # 2. Reusable Template Mixins (Optional)
    templates:
      - visual_legendary_relic
      - economy_tier_legendary

    # 3. Durability & Expiration Limits
    permanent: false
    time: 86400           # Duration in seconds (or human format '24h', '7d'). 0 = no time limit
    uses: 10              # Maximum craft count before the blueprint expires. 0 = unlimited

    # 4. Vault Economy Integration
    price: 15000.0        # Purchase price in catalog (/cb item list) and /cb buy
    sell_price: 3750.0    # Refund value when selling back to the catalog

    # 5. In-Game Physical Item Representation
    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP     # FILLED_MAP, PAPER, BOOK, NETHER_STAR, etc.
      custom_model_data: 2004  # CustomModelData integer for resource pack models
      glowing: true            # Enchantment shimmer sheen without lore clutter

    # 6. Map Visual Drafting Aesthetics (Active when material is FILLED_MAP)
    map:
      theme: forge             # Procedural theme or image in images/backgrounds/
      frame: rosette           # Corner architecture: bracket, chamfer, diamond, runic, rosette, star, none
      badge: smithing          # Workstation badge: crafting, anvil, brewing, smithing, furnace, none
      icon_scale: 2            # Integer scale (1 to 4) using sharp nearest-neighbor interpolation
      drop_shadow: true        # Subtle 2px ambient occlusion drop shadow behind item sprite
      item_outline:
        enabled: true
        width: 2               # Continuous contour outline width in pixels (1 to 8)
        color: "rainbow"       # 'rainbow', hex '#ffd700', or gradient
        opacity: 100           # Opacity percentage (1 to 100)

    # 7. MiniMessage Lore Description Card
    lore:
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>-----------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{target_item}</white>"
      - "<gray>Remaining Forges:</gray> <yellow><bold>{uses} / 10</bold></yellow>"
      - "<gray>Licensing Time:</gray> <aqua>{time}</aqua>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>-----------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<yellow>Catalog Price:</yellow> <green>${price}</green>"
      - "<yellow>Scrap Value:</yellow> <gold>${sell_price}</gold>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>-----------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<dark_gray>Hold map in hand and Right-Click to memorize.</dark_gray>"

    # 8. Extensible Metadata Block (Custom Scripts & Hooks)
    extra:
      tier: "MYTHIC"
      category: "HEAVY_WEAPONS"
      tradeable: false

docs.title: File Organization & Lexical Scope
docs.text:
You can organize your YAML files into any directory hierarchy inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/:

plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/
├── 00_templates.yml           # Global templates (visible to all directories)
├── weapons/
│   ├── swords.yml             # Single blueprints
│   ├── axes.yml
│   └── legendary/
│       └── mythic_blades.yml
├── armor/
│   ├── sets.yml               # Package blueprints (full sets)
│   └── shields.yml
└── consumables/
    ├── potions.yml            # Alchemy brewing blueprints
    └── enchanted_books.yml    # Anvil enchantment blueprints

docs.title: 1. Deterministic First-Win ID Collision Rule
docs.text:
If two blueprints in different files (or within the same file) declare the identical lowercase ID (e.g. starter_sword in both weapons/swords.yml and kits/beginner.yml): * The first file encountered during alphabetical directory traversal wins and registers the blueprint. * The duplicate definition is ignored, and a warning is printed to the console: 

[CraftingBlueprints] Duplicate blueprint ID 'starter_sword' in 'kits/beginner.yml' ignored: already defined in 'weapons/swords.yml'.

docs.title: 2. Atomic Fail-Safe on Syntax Errors
docs.text:
• If any YAML file contains malformed syntax (unbalanced quotes, illegal tab indentation, broken blocks), the reload process triggers an immediate atomic abort.
  • Zero Database Modifications: No blueprints are inserted, updated, or pruned.
  • The previous working database state remains 100% intact, protecting your live server from broken configurations.

docs.title: 3. Non-Fatal Version Skipping
docs.text: • If a blueprint specifies an item, material, or recipe that does not exist on your server version (e.g. MACE or WIND_CHARGE on Paper 1.20.4), the plugin safely skips that individual item without aborting the reload or deleting existing records. All other valid blueprints in the file load normally.

docs.title: Dry-Run Validation (/cb validate)
docs.text:
Always verify your files before or after editing:

/cb validate

The validator performs comprehensive linting: * Verifies Bukkit material, potion, and enchantment identifiers against the active server version. * Validates hex colors and named color palette references. * Detects circular dependencies and unresolved template references. * Emits Levenshtein distance "Did you mean?" suggestions for minor typos (e.g., roseta $\rightarrow$ rosette).

docs.title: Custom Items, CustomModelData & Plugin Interoperability
docs.text:
Modern Minecraft RPG and survival networks rarely rely solely on vanilla items. Plugins such as ItemsAdder, Oraxen, Nexo, MMOItems, EcoItems, and MythicMobs generate hundreds of custom weapons, armor sets, and tools that share identical base vanilla materials (e.g. DIAMOND_SWORD, BOW, PAPER) differentiated only by CustomModelData, persistent NBT/PDC tags, or custom crafting recipe keys.

CraftingBlueprints features an extensible ItemIdentifierProvider Service Provider Interface (SPI) that inspects and gates custom items natively without collisions.

docs.title: 1. CustomModelData on Physical Blueprint Items
docs.text:
If your resource pack includes custom 3D models for physical blueprint items (such as ancient parchment scrolls, magical stone tablets, or holographic holocrons):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  ancient_katana_scroll:
    blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD
    name: "<gold><bold>Ancient Katana Scroll</bold></gold>"

    # Physical item representation
    item:
      material: PAPER
      custom_model_data: 5012   # Matches your resource pack CustomModelData predicate
      glowing: true

    lore:
      - "<gray>A sacred parchment detailing the</gray>"
      - "<gray>forging of traditional katanas.</gray>"

When a player receives this blueprint, their Minecraft client renders the custom 3D model corresponding to CustomModelData: 5012.

docs.title: 2. Gating External Plugin Items (ItemsAdder, Oraxen, Nexo)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints hooks into external item plugins using an ordered SPI hierarchy. You can reference custom items directly in the blueprint: target field using namespaced prefixes:

docs.title: 1. ItemsAdder Compatibility (ia:)
docs.text:
Requires the ItemsAdder plugin. Uses the ia:<namespace:id> prefix:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  ruby_broadsword_blueprint:
    # Target ItemsAdder custom item
    blueprint: "ia:rpgweapons:ruby_broadsword"
    name: "<red><bold>Ruby Broadsword Blueprint</bold></red>"
    permanent: true

    map:
      theme: dwarven_magma
      frame: rosette
      badge: smithing

docs.title: 2. Oraxen Compatibility (oraxen:)
docs.text:
Requires the Oraxen plugin. Uses the oraxen:<id> prefix:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  mythril_pickaxe_blueprint:
    # Target Oraxen custom item ID
    blueprint: "oraxen:mythril_pickaxe"
    name: "<aqua><bold>Mythril Pickaxe Blueprint</bold></aqua>"
    permanent: true

    map:
      theme: technical_slate
      frame: bracket
      badge: crafting

docs.title: 3. Nexo Compatibility (nexo:)
docs.text:
Requires the Nexo plugin. Uses the nexo:<id> prefix:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  amethyst_spear_blueprint:
    # Target Nexo custom item ID
    blueprint: "nexo:amethyst_spear"
    name: "<light_purple><bold>Amethyst Spear Blueprint</bold></light_purple>"
    permanent: true

docs.title: 4. MMOItems Compatibility (mmoitems:)
docs.text:
Requires MMOItems. Uses the mmoitems:<TYPE>:<ID> format:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  excalibur_relic_blueprint:
    blueprint: "mmoitems:SWORD:EXCALIBUR"
    name: "<gold><bold>Holy Excalibur Blueprint</bold></gold>"
    permanent: true

docs.title: 5. EcoItems & MythicMobs (Native PDC Hooks)
docs.text:
• EcoItems: ecoitems:<id> (e.g. ecoitems:titan_axe)
  • MythicMobs: mythicmobs:<id> (e.g. mythicmobs:skeleton_king_crown)

docs.title: 3. Pure Vanilla CustomModelData Matching
docs.text:
If your server uses custom items via vanilla datapacks or simple CustomModelData without a heavy plugin framework:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  obsidian_scythe_blueprint:
    # Target material with CustomModelData selector
    blueprint: "diamond_hoe@custom_model_data:1042"
    name: "<dark_purple><bold>Obsidian Scythe Blueprint</bold></dark_purple>"
    permanent: true

CraftingBlueprints verifies that the crafted item matches both Material.DIAMOND_HOE and CustomModelData == 1042. Standard diamond hoes crafted by players remain unaffected.

docs.title: 4. Gating Custom Datapack Recipes (recipe:)
docs.text:
To gate custom crafting table recipes registered via vanilla datapacks or custom crafting engines:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  custom_saddle_recipe:
    # Target recipe namespaced key
    blueprint: "recipe:customcrafting:leather_saddle"
    name: "<gold>Craftable Saddle Blueprint</gold>"
    permanent: true

docs.title: 5. Economy Safety Policy: fallback-to-vanilla
docs.text:
In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

item-matching:
  enabled: true
  fallback-to-vanilla: true

docs.title: Why is this crucial for server balance?
docs.text: Imagine your server has 50 custom swords registered in ItemsAdder that use DIAMOND_SWORD as their base material. * If an administrator creates an explicit blueprint for ia:rpgweapons:flame_blade, but forgets to configure blueprints for the other 49 custom swords: * With fallback-to-vanilla: true: The plugin checks if the base vanilla material (diamond_sword) is restricted in Whitelist Mode. Since it is, the unconfigured custom swords safely fall back to requiring the base Diamond Sword blueprint. Players cannot bypass your progression! * With fallback-to-vanilla: false: Unconfigured custom swords would be freely craftable by anyone with raw ingredients.

docs.title: 6. Extensible Metadata (extra)
docs.text:
The extra: mapping allows you to attach custom key-value pairs to any blueprint. This data is preserved in memory and can be queried by external plugins, Skript, or Denizen:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  shadow_dagger:
    blueprint: IRON_SWORD
    extra:
      required_combat_level: 45
      rpg_class: "ASSASSIN"
      tradeable: false
      custom_stat_multiplier: 1.25

docs.title: Durability, Expiration Limits & Usage Modes
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints provides three distinct durability models to balance your server's crafting economy and progression. You can configure recipes to be Permanent, Craft-Count Limited (Uses), or Time-Limited (Timer Expiration), or combine them into hybrid licensing models.

docs.title: 1. Permanent Blueprints (permanent: true)
docs.text:
The player learns the recipe once and retains the permanent ability to craft it indefinitely:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  iron_pickaxe_mastery:
    blueprint: IRON_PICKAXE
    name: "<white>Iron Pickaxe Schematic</white>"

    # Permanent unlock: never expires, unlimited crafts
    permanent: true
    time: 0
    uses: 0

    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: false

    map:
      theme: technical
      frame: bracket
      badge: crafting

    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{target_item}</white>"
      - "<gray>Duration:</gray> <green>Permanent</green>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click to permanently memorize this recipe.</dark_gray>"
  • Best For: Milestone survival progression (e.g. unlocking Iron, Diamond, or Netherite tiers permanently).
  • Memory Invariant: Stored once in the player's account database profile with no background timers or counters.

docs.title: 2. Craft-Count Limited Blueprints (uses: 3)
docs.text:
The player unlocks the recipe, but each completed craft decrements an internal usage counter. When the counter reaches zero, the recipe is consumed and automatically locked again:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  dragon_slayer_scroll:
    blueprint: NETHERITE_SWORD
    name: "<gradient:#9900EE:#FF0055><bold>Scroll of the Dragon Slayer</bold></gradient>"

    # Limited crafts: expires after exactly 3 crafts
    permanent: false
    time: 0
    uses: 3

    item:
      material: PAPER
      glowing: true

    map:
      theme: runic
      frame: runic
      badge: smithing
      stamp:
        show: true
        style: wax_seal
        text: "3x"

    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{target_item}</white>"
      - "<gray>Remaining Forges:</gray> <yellow><bold>{uses} / 3 crafts</bold></yellow>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Allows forging up to 3 blades before dissolving.</yellow>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click in hand to bind this knowledge.</dark_gray>"
  • Best For: Mythic weapons, dungeon boss drop scrolls, MMORPG magic forge tokens, or event prizes where you want to prevent players from mass-producing items and crashing the server economy.
  • Stacking Behavior: If a player consumes another 3-use scroll while having 2 uses remaining, the plugin stacks the uses to 5.

docs.title: 3. Time-Limited Blueprints (time: 86400 or time: 24h)
docs.text:
The player unlocks the recipe for a temporary duration measured from the exact moment of unlocking. While active, the player can craft unlimited items. When the timer expires, the recipe is automatically revoked:

Raw Integer SecondsHuman Duration String 
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  weekend_crossbow_pass:
    blueprint: CROSSBOW
    name: "<gold><bold>Weekend Tournament Crossbow License</bold></gold>"

    # Exactly 24 hours (86,400 seconds)
    permanent: false
    time: 86400
    uses: 0

    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    map:
      theme: royal
      frame: diamond
      badge: crafting
      stamp:
        show: true
        style: clock
        text: "24h"

    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{target_item}</white>"
      - "<gray>License Duration:</gray> <aqua>{time}</aqua>"
      - "<gray>Craft Count:</gray> <green>Unlimited</green>"

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  weekly_alchemist_license:
    blueprint: POTION
    name: "<light_purple><bold>7-Day Master Alchemist License</bold></light_purple>"

    # Human-readable 7 days duration
    permanent: false
    time: 7d
    uses: 0

    item:
      material: BOOK
      glowing: true

    lore:
      - "<gray>Permit Duration:</gray> <aqua>{time}</aqua>"
      - "<gray>Craft Count:</gray> <green>Unlimited</green>"

docs.title: Supported Duration Units
docs.text: The duration parser accepts human strings or raw integer seconds: * 45s $\rightarrow$ 45 seconds * 30m $\rightarrow$ 30 minutes (1,800 seconds) * 12h $\rightarrow$ 12 hours (43,200 seconds) * 86400 or 24h $\rightarrow$ 24 hours (86,400 seconds) * 7d $\rightarrow$ 7 days (604,800 seconds) * 30d $\rightarrow$ 30 days (2,592,000 seconds) * 0 $\rightarrow$ No temporal expiration.

docs.title: 4. Hybrid Licensing (Combined Time & Uses)
docs.text:
You can specify both time and uses on a single blueprint. Whichever limit is reached first will expire and lock the recipe:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  seasonal_relic_shield:
    blueprint: SHIELD
    name: "<gradient:#00AAFF:#00FFAA><bold>Seasonal Aegis Shield</bold></gradient>"

    # Expires in 7 days OR after 5 crafts, whichever happens first
    permanent: false
    time: 7d
    uses: 5

    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    map:
      theme: nautical_astrolabe
      frame: star
      badge: anvil

    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{target_item}</white>"
      - "<gray>Remaining Forges:</gray> <yellow>{uses} / 5</yellow>"
      - "<gray>Time Limit:</gray> <aqua>{time}</aqua>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Expires after 5 crafts or when time runs out.</yellow>"

docs.title: Shift-Craft Capacity & Anti-Exploit Math
docs.text:
In standard Minecraft plugins, shift-clicking crafting recipes can cause severe desynchronization, allowing players to duplicate items or craft 64 items while only deducting 1 use from their counter.

CraftingBlueprints eliminates this exploit via an atomic Shift-Craft Rule Engine (ShiftCraftMath.kt):

  1. Matrix Ingredient Capacity: Evaluates the minimum ingredient count across all matrix slots to calculate maximum possible crafts: $$\text{MaxMatrixCrafts} = \min_{s \in \text{slots}}(\text{amount}_s)$$
  2. Inventory Destination Capacity: Evaluates the player's empty inventory slots and partial stacks to determine the exact number of crafted items that can fit safely without overflowing: $$\text{MaxSpaceCrafts} = \left\lfloor \frac{\text{FreeSpace}}{\text{RecipeYield}} \right\rfloor$$
  3. Usage Bound: Evaluates the remaining uses on the player's active blueprint: $$\text{CraftCount} = \min(\text{MaxMatrixCrafts}, \text{MaxSpaceCrafts}, \text{RemainingUses})$$
  4. Atomic Execution: If a player with 2 remaining uses shift-clicks a recipe with 64 iron ingots in the matrix, the engine crafts exactly 2 items, deducts exactly 2 uses, locks the recipe, and leaves the remaining 62 iron ingots untouched in the crafting table.

docs.title: How Players Track Active Uses & Timers
docs.text:
Players have multiple real-time tools to monitor their active blueprints:

  1. Personal Dashboard (/cb menu): Shows all active recipes, remaining craft counts, and live countdown timers (e.g. Expires in 3d 14h).
  2. Catalog Inspection (/cb item list): Hovering over any blueprint displays dynamic status badges:
  3. Unlocked (Permanent)
  4. Active: 3/5 Uses (Limited)
  5. Locked
  6. PlaceholderAPI Variables:
  7. %craftingblueprints_uses_<id>%: Returns remaining uses (or unlimited).
  8. %craftingblueprints_time_<id>%: Formatted remaining time (e.g. 23h 12m).
  9. %craftingblueprints_is_unlocked_<id>%: Returns true or false.

docs.title: Blueprint Packs, Packages & Permission Groups
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints provides multiple ways to manage collections of recipes together: 1. Multi-Recipe Packages (packages:): Single physical or virtual items that unlock an entire collection of recipes simultaneously (such as a full armor set). 2. Mystery Blueprints (mysteries:): Probability-weighted loot scrolls that roll a random reward from a pool upon right-click. 3. Permission Groups (groups: in config.yml): Virtual permission tiers assigned to player ranks via LuckPerms (craftingblueprints.group.<id>).

docs.title: 1. Multi-Recipe Packages (packages:)
docs.text: A Package Blueprint is an item that, when unlocked, grants multiple recipes at once. It is ideal for complete armor sets, tool lines, builder palettes, and class starter kits.

docs.title: Full Armor Set Example (Netherite Vanguard Pack)
docs.text:
In any blueprint file (e.g. plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/armor_packs.yml):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
packages:
  netherite_vanguard_pack:
    name: "<gradient:#333333:#888888><bold>Netherite Vanguard Armor Set</bold></gradient>"

    # Physical representation in inventory and shop
    item:
      material: BOOK
      custom_model_data: 3001
      glowing: true

    # Economy settings for Vault shop
    price: 65000.0
    sell_price: 15000.0

    # Map portfolio aesthetics if rendered as map
    map:
      theme: forge
      frame: rosette
      badge: smithing
      stamp:
        show: true
        style: plaque

docs.title: 2. Mystery Blueprints & Crate Rolls (mysteries:)
docs.text:
Mystery Blueprints act as self-contained loot crates or ancient arcane scrolls. When a player right-clicks the item, the plugin rolls against a probability-weighted reward pool:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
mysteries:
  ancient_dungeon_scroll:
    name: "<yellow><bold>Ancient Dungeon Mystery Scroll</bold></yellow>"

    item:
      material: PAPER
      custom_model_data: 4001
      glowing: true

    price: 10000.0
    sell_price: 2000.0

    pool:
      # Common roll (Weight 60)

        weight: 60

        permanent: true

      - blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD

        name: "<aqua>Diamond Blade Blueprint</aqua>"
        permanent: true

      - id: netherite_vanguard_pack

docs.title: 3. Permission Groups in config.yml (groups:)
docs.text:
Unlike physical packages that players hold in their inventories, Permission Groups are virtual recipe permissions tied to LuckPerms player ranks via craftingblueprints.group.<id>.

Configured in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

groups:
  # Base default rank: basic survival items
  default:
    name: "Default"
    blueprints:
      - stick
      - ".*planks"
      - ".*door"
      - ".*fence"
      - ".*stairs"
      - ".*slab"
      - "wooden.*"
      - "stone.*"

  # VIP Rank: inherits all Default recipes automatically!
  vip:
    name: "VIP"
    inherits:
      - default
    blueprints:
      - iron_ingot
      - "iron_.*"
      - "shield"
      - "crossbow"

  # Pro Rank: multi-level inheritance (VIP + Default)
  pro:
    name: "Pro"
    inherits:
      - vip
    blueprints:
      - "*gold*"
      - "diamond_.*"
      - "netherite_.*"

docs.title: Pattern Matching in Groups:
docs.text:
• Literal Materials: stick, iron_ingot, shield.
  • Wildcard Globs: *gold* matches anything containing the word gold.
  • Regular Expressions: iron_.* matches all iron tools and armor; .*planks matches all wood plank types.
  • Potion Category: potion:strength.* matches Strength brewing recipes.
  • Enchantment Category: enchantment:mending matches Mending anvil combinations.

docs.title: Granting Groups via LuckPerms:
docs.text:
To grant a group to a player rank, assign the node craftingblueprints.group.<id>:

# Grant VIP recipe pack to the vip LuckPerms group
lp group vip permission set craftingblueprints.group.vip true

# Grant Pro recipe pack to the pro LuckPerms group
lp group pro permission set craftingblueprints.group.pro true

docs.text: CraftingBlueprints features an advanced in-game map rendering engine that composites photorealistic technical drafting schematics, banknote-grade Guilloché security borders, procedural item outlines, and custom artwork directly onto in-game Minecraft Maps (Material.FILLED_MAP).

docs.title: Enabling Map Graphics
docs.text:

# Enable fabulous BlueprintsItems with images on maps

docs.title: Flyweight Map Registry & Anti-Desync Architecture
docs.text:
When images-on-maps is enabled, CraftingBlueprints protects your server performance and disk space through its Flyweight Map Registry:

  1. Zero World Save Bloat: In vanilla Minecraft, creating maps allocates a new Map ID for every item, creating thousands of duplicate map_<id>.dat files in world/data/. CraftingBlueprints computes a deterministic VisualKey for each visual configuration and assigns exactly one MapView per distinct visual render, regardless of whether 10 or 10,000 players own that blueprint.
  2. Cross-Server Map Virtualization: In multi-server networks (Bungee/Velocity), Map ID 104 on Server A might be an Excalibur sword, while on Server B it is the spawn hub map. The physical item's PDC stores the normalized visual_key. When a player transfers between servers, the plugin's MapRelinkListener dynamically re-links the item to the local canonical Map ID in-place, guaranteeing blueprints never turn blank or corrupt local maps.
  3. Container & Item Frame Persistence: Blueprints stored in chests, shulker boxes, or displayed in Item Frames retain their renderers across server restarts without reverting to vanilla terrain maps.
  4. Sub-Tick Rendering Performance: All image quantization executes on asynchronous background threads, pre-quantizing images into native byte[16384] palette buffers. Blitting on the server tick loop executes in < 0.02 milliseconds, maintaining buttery-smooth 20.0 TPS.

docs.title: Reusable Templates (Mixins) & Cascading Precedence
docs.text:
When managing servers with dozens or hundreds of blueprints, retyping the same pricing, visual themes, lore cards, and durability rules for every single recipe introduces configuration bloat and maintenance errors.

CraftingBlueprints features an object-oriented Template Composition Engine (Mixins) that allows server administrators to define modular template blocks once and compose them across multiple blueprints.

docs.title: 1. Defining Reusable Templates (templates:)
docs.text:
Templates are non-instantiated blueprint modules declared under the root templates: section of any YAML file in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
templates:
  # Module 1: Visual styling for ancient magic scrolls
  visual_ancient_scroll:
    item:
      material: PAPER
      custom_model_data: 1001
      glowing: true
    map:
      theme: parchment_aged
      frame: runic
      badge: crafting

  # Module 2: Visual styling for legendary forge relics
  visual_legendary_relic:
    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true
    map:
      theme: forge
      frame: rosette
      badge: smithing
      item_outline:
        enabled: true
        width: 2
        color: "rainbow"

  # Module 3: Economy pricing tier (Epic)
  economy_tier_epic:
    price: 15000.0
    sell_price: 3750.0
    extra:
      tier: "EPIC"
      currency: "VAULT"

  # Module 4: 3-Craft durability limit mixin
  usage_three_crafts:
    permanent: false
    time: 0
    uses: 3

  # Module 5: Permanent unlimited usage mixin
  usage_permanent:
    permanent: true
    time: 0
    uses: 0

docs.title: 2. Composing Templates on Blueprints
docs.text:
To apply templates to a blueprint, list their IDs under templates: (or single string template:):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  titan_greatsword:
    blueprint: NETHERITE_SWORD
    name: "<gradient:#FF0000:#FFAA00><bold>Titan Greatsword Blueprint</bold></gradient>"

    # Multi-template mixin composition
    templates:
      - visual_legendary_relic
      - economy_tier_epic
      - usage_three_crafts

    # Specific local override (Blueprint overrides Template 3):
    uses: 5

docs.title: 3. Mixin Inheritance Precedence Rules
docs.text:
When a blueprint inherits multiple templates, CraftingBlueprints resolves configurations using strict left-to-right cascading precedence:

$$\text{Parent Folders } \texttt{default:} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{Folder } \texttt{default:} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{File } \texttt{file_default:} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{Template 1} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{Template 2} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{Blueprint Local Config}$$

                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │        1. Inherited Folder Defaults          │
                │        (From root blueprints/ downward)      │
                └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                       ▼
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │        2. Current Folder default:            │
                └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                       ▼
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │        3. Current File file_default:         │
                └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                       ▼
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │        4. Template 1 (First Mixin)           │
                └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                       ▼
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │        5. Template 2 (Second Mixin)          │
                │            (Overrides Template 1)            │
                └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                       ▼
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │        6. Blueprint Local Configuration      │
                │             (HIGHEST PRECEDENCE)             │
                └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                       ▼
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │            Final Merged Blueprint            │
                └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Precedence Invariants:
docs.text:
1. Blueprint Local Wins: Any property defined explicitly on the blueprint itself (e.g. uses: 5, price: 25000.0, or local name:) always takes absolute precedence over all templates and defaults.
  2. Template Order (Right Overrides Left): If Template 1 defines price: 10000.0 and Template 2 defines price: 15000.0, Template 2 wins because it is evaluated later in the list: $$\text{Blueprint} > \text{Template 2} > \text{Template 1}$$
  3. Dictionaries & Maps (item:, map:, extra:): Deep-merged recursively. If Template 1 sets item.material: FILLED_MAP and Template 2 sets item.glowing: true, the resulting item will have both material: FILLED_MAP and glowing: true.
  4. Lists (lore:, blueprints:, pool:): Replaced entirely by the latest non-empty list declared in the cascade.
  5. Scalars (name:, price:, permanent:, uses:, time:): Overwritten by the latest declared non-null scalar.

docs.title: 4. Hierarchical Lexical Scoping
docs.text:
Templates are not flat global variables; they follow downward directory scoping:

  1. Global Templates (Root Scope): Any template declared in a YAML file at the root of plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/ (e.g. blueprints/00_templates.yml) is globally visible to all blueprints across all folders and subfolders.
  2. Folder-Scoped Templates: A template declared in blueprints/weapons/templates.yml is visible only to files inside blueprints/weapons/ and its subdirectories (e.g. weapons/swords/, weapons/axes/). It cannot be accessed by armor/ or root files.
  3. Template Shadowing (Nearest-Ancestor): If a template named tier_epic is declared at both the root level and inside weapons/, blueprints in weapons/ will inherit the local weapons/tier_epic definition.

docs.title: 5. Folder & File Defaults (default: & file_default:)
docs.text:
To apply settings across an entire folder without repeatedly typing templates: on every item, use defaults:

# Inside blueprints/weapons/swords.yml

# File-Level Default: applies to all blueprints in this file
file_default:
  price: 7500.0
  item:
    material: FILLED_MAP
    glowing: true
  map:
    theme: technical
    frame: bracket

singles:
  iron_blade:
    blueprint: IRON_SWORD
    name: "<white>Iron Blade</white>"
    # Automatically inherits price: 7500.0 and technical map theme!

  diamond_blade:
    blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD
    name: "<aqua>Diamond Blade</aqua>"
    price: 15000.0 # Overrides the file default price

docs.title: Cutting Off Inheritance (inherit: false)
docs.text:
If you have an isolated file (such as admin event items) and want to discard all inherited folder defaults:

file_default:
  inherit: false    # Discards all ancestor folder defaults; starts from clean slate
  price: 0.0
  extra:
    category: "admin_only"

docs.title: /cb give <player> <blueprint_id> [amount]
docs.text:
Grants physical blueprint items directly to a target player: * Quantity Bounds: The amount parameter strictly requires a positive integer between 1 and 2304 (the maximum physical capacity of a player inventory: $36 \text{ slots} \times 64 \text{ items}$). Negative numbers, 0, non-numeric strings, or exorbitant numbers are rejected immediately with localized error feedback. * Physical Overflow Safety: When giving items to a player whose inventory is full, CraftingBlueprints uses an atomic safe-drop protocol. Instead of dropping items into the void or deleting them, leftover items are dropped safely into the world directly at the player's location (world.dropItem(...)).

# Give Steve 1 Ancient Netherite Battleaxe blueprint
/cb give Steve ancient_netherite_axe 1

# Give Alex 5 3-use magic scrolls via console
/cb give Alex astral_blade_scroll 5

docs.title: /cb reload [all|blueprints|config|lang]
docs.text:
Hot-reloads plugin subsystems instantly on live servers without disconnects or lag spikes:

  • /cb reload all: Full reload of config.yml, language files, and declarative YAML blueprints.
  • /cb reload blueprints: Re-reads and recompiles all files in blueprints/, updates the shared database, and emits a network sync signal to worker nodes.
  • /cb reload config: Reloads config.yml (groups, restrictions, crafter rules, cache).
  • /cb reload lang: Hot-reloads messages_en.yml and messages_es.yml translations.

docs.title: /cb validate
docs.text: Executes an offline dry-run verification across all blueprint files in blueprints/: * Zero Database Modifications: Performs no database inserts, updates, or prunings. * Semantic Verification: Verifies that every Bukkit Material, PotionType, and Enchantment exists on the current server version. * Visual Key Linting: Recursively validates map: blocks against valid themes, frames, and badges. * Levenshtein Suggestions: Automatically emits helpful "Did you mean?" suggestions for minor typos (e.g. roseta $\rightarrow$ rosette). * Line-Number Error Context: In the event of a syntax error, reports the exact file path, line number, column, and error description.

docs.title: Recipe Group Permissions (craftingblueprints.group.<id>)
docs.text:
In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml, you define permission groups (e.g., default, vip, pro, alchemist):

groups:
  vip:
    name: "VIP"
    inherits:
      - default
    blueprints:
      - "iron_.*"
      - "shield"
      - "crossbow"

To grant all recipes in the vip group to your VIP rank, assign the node:

craftingblueprints.group.vip

Because vip inherits default, players with this permission automatically unlock all recipes in default as well.

docs.title: Production LuckPerms Configurations
docs.text:
Below are ready-to-use configurations for standard server ranks:

LuckPerms CLI CommandsYAML Format (groups.yml)

Run these commands in your server console or in-game as an administrator:

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Default Players (default rank)
# --------------------------------------------------
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.menu true
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.return true
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.item.list true
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.info true
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.group.default true

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. VIP Players (vip rank)
# --------------------------------------------------
lp group vip permission set craftingblueprints.group.vip true

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Moderators & Staff (moderator rank)
# --------------------------------------------------
lp group moderator permission set craftingblueprints.status true
lp group moderator permission set craftingblueprints.bypass.ownership true

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Server Administrators (admin rank)
# --------------------------------------------------
lp group admin permission set craftingblueprints.* true

If you manage LuckPerms via file storage (plugins/LuckPerms/yaml-storage/groups.yml):

default:
  permissions:
    - craftingblueprints.menu:
        value: true
    - craftingblueprints.return:
        value: true
    - craftingblueprints.item.list:
        value: true
    - craftingblueprints.info:
        value: true
    - craftingblueprints.group.default:
        value: true

vip:
  parents:
    - default
  permissions:
    - craftingblueprints.group.vip:
        value: true

moderator:
  parents:
    - default
  permissions:
    - craftingblueprints.status:
        value: true
    - craftingblueprints.bypass.ownership:
        value: true

admin:
  permissions:
    - craftingblueprints.*:
        value: true

docs.title: Network & World-Specific Permissions
docs.text:
On multi-server networks or multi-world servers where crafting progression differs between worlds (e.g. Survival vs Creative):

# Allow catalog access only in the survival world
lp group default permission set craftingblueprints.item.list true world=survival

# Restrict admin status check to the management hub server
lp group moderator permission set craftingblueprints.status true server=lobby

docs.title: Master Configuration Guide (config.yml)
docs.text: The primary configuration file for CraftingBlueprints is located at plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml. This guide provides an exhaustive, line-by-line reference for every configuration key, explaining its exact in-game behavior, recommended values for production servers, and operational gotchas.

docs.title: Annotated Production config.yml
docs.text:
# ============================================================ #
#             CRAFTINGBLUEPRINTS MASTER CONFIG                 #
# ============================================================ #

# Internal schema version. Do not modify manually.
config-version: 4

# Enable verbose debug logging in console.
# Keep set to 'false' in production to maintain a clean console and high performance.
debug: false

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Core Gameplay Rules
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Restrict physical blueprint items to their original recipient UUID.
# - true: Prevents players from trading, dropping, or sharing physical blueprint maps.
#         Only the player whose UUID is stamped on the item may hold and learn it.
# - false: Blueprints are completely tradeable physical commodities.
item-ownership: true

# Render custom 128x128 pixel visual schematics on in-game maps (Material.FILLED_MAP).
# When true, physical blueprints display thematic backgrounds, borders, and item sprites.
images-on-maps: true

# Allow server operators (/op) to bypass all recipe restrictions.
# - true: Server operators can craft, smelt, brew, and enchant any locked recipe.
# - false: Operators are subject to the same blueprint progression as normal players.
op-bypass: true

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Database Storage Configuration
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Storage engine backend: 'sqlite' or 'mysql' (default: sqlite)
database-type: sqlite

# Database name (for SQLite: filename without .db; for MySQL: target database name)
database-name: crafting_blueprints

# MySQL Connection Parameters (Ignored when database-type is 'sqlite')
database-host: localhost
database-port: 3306
database-user: root
database-password: "your_strong_password"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Declarative File Management & Synchronization
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

file-management:
  # Multi-Server Golden Rule:
  # - true: ONLY on the designated Primary Management Node (e.g. Hub/Lobby).
  #         Imports local YAML files into the shared database and prunes deleted items.
  # - false: On ALL Worker Nodes (Survival, Skyblock, Factions).
  #          Worker nodes load blueprints strictly from the shared MySQL database.
  sync-from-files: false

  # Directory relative to plugins/CraftingBlueprints/ where blueprint YAMLs reside.
  directory: "blueprints"

  # Directory where inactive preset packages, zip bundles, and folders are stored.
  presets-directory: "presets"

  # If true, file-managed blueprints that are deleted from YAML files on disk
  # are automatically pruned from the database during reload.
  # Manually created in-game blueprints are NEVER pruned by this option.
  prune-deleted: true

  # Automatic live file watcher (hot-reloads when files change on disk)
  auto-reload:
    enabled: true
    # Debounce delay in milliseconds to prevent reading files while still being saved by editors
    debounce-delay-ms: 1500

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# In-Game Blueprint Exporter & Rolling Backups
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

in-game-export:
  # Automatically export blueprints created in-game via GUI or commands into a YAML file
  enabled: true

  # Automatically generate diagnostic text reports (minecraft_recipes.txt,
  # groups_recipes.txt, registered_blueprints.txt, system_summary.txt) in exports/ on reload
  auto-export-on-reload: true

  # Subdirectory relative to plugins/CraftingBlueprints/
  directory: "exports"
  file-name: "manual_blueprints.yml"

  # Rolling backups of exported manual blueprints
  backups:
    enabled: true
    # Backup interval (e.g., 30m, 1h, 6h, 1d)
    interval: 1h
    # Maximum number of rolling backup files to retain in exports/backups/
    max-count: 5

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Permission Groups & Recipe Inheritance
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Permission groups unlock categories of recipes via: craftingblueprints.group.<id>
# Supports direct material names, regex (.*planks), wildcards (*gold*),
# potion effects (potion:strength.*), enchantments (enchantment:mending),
# and multi-parent inheritance (inherits: [groupA, groupB]).
groups:
  default:
    name: "Default"
    blueprints:
      - stick
      - ".*planks"
      - ".*door"
      - ".*fence"
      - ".*stairs"
      - ".*slab"
      - ".*pressure_plate"
      - ".*button"
      - ".*sign"
      - ".*chest"
      - ".*bed"
      - "wooden.*"
      - "stone.*"

  vip:
    name: "VIP"
    inherits:
      - default
    blueprints:
      - iron_ingot
      - "iron_.*"
      - "shield"
      - "crossbow"

  pro:
    name: "Pro"
    inherits:
      - vip
    blueprints:
      - "*gold*"
      - "diamond_.*"
      - "netherite_.*"

  alchemist:
    name: "Alchemist"
    blueprints:
      - "brewing_stand"
      - "glass_bottle"
      - "potion:.*"
      - "healing.*"
      - "speed.*"
      - "strength.*"

  enchanter:
    name: "Enchanter"
    blueprints:
      - "enchanting_table"
      - "anvil"
      - "enchantment:.*"
      - "silk_touch"
      - "unbreaking.*"
      - "mending"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Cache & Memory Management
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

cache:
  # Blueprint items cache in RAM
  items:
    max-size: 1500

  # Player profiles cache in RAM
  players:
    # Maximum active player profiles kept in memory simultaneously
    max-size: 500
    # Grace period in seconds before an offline player's profile is evicted
    disconnect-grace-period-seconds: 5
    # Scavenger task interval in seconds to purge idle offline profiles
    orphan-scavenger-interval-seconds: 30
    # Threshold window in seconds where an offline player is considered active if queried
    active-access-threshold-seconds: 30

  # Map graphics byte buffer cache
  maps:
    # Maximum pre-quantized 128x128 palette byte buffers (16 KB each) cached in RAM
    max-cached-buffers: 500

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# PlaceholderAPI Integration
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

placeholderapi:
  # Direct read-only database query when a requested blueprint or player is not in RAM cache.
  # - false (recommended for optimal TPS): returns default values ("false", "0") immediately
  #   and warms cache asynchronously in the background.
  # - true: queries database synchronously on cache miss.
  query-database-on-cache-miss: false

  # Allow synchronous database queries on the server main thread for placeholders.
  # Default: false (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED). Prevents server tick drops when scoreboards refresh.
  allow-sync-queries-on-main-thread: false

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Automated Crafter Interception (Minecraft 1.21+)
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

crafter:
  # If true, redstone-powered Crafter blocks are blocked from crafting blueprint-locked recipes.
  # If false, Crafters bypass player checks and craft all recipes automatically.
  block-restricted: true

  # Play a dispenser fail click sound and smoke particles at the Crafter when crafting is blocked.
  fail-effect: true

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Custom Item Matcher SPI (External Plugins)
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

item-matching:
  # Master toggle for custom item inspection SPI
  enabled: true

  # Fallback policy: if a custom item (e.g. ItemsAdder/Nexo weapon) does NOT have
  # its own custom blueprint, should it fall back to requiring the base vanilla material blueprint?
  # - true (recommended): Prevents players from crafting OP custom swords just because
  #   an administrator forgot to write an explicit custom blueprint for them.
  # - false: Custom items without explicit blueprints are freely craftable.
  fallback-to-vanilla: true

  providers:
    itemsadder:
      enabled: true
      priority: 100
      prefix: "ia"

    nexo:
      enabled: true
      priority: 100
      prefix: "nexo"

    oraxen:
      enabled: true
      priority: 100
      prefix: "oraxen"

    mmoitems:
      enabled: true
      priority: 100
      prefix: "mmoitems"

    ecoitems:
      enabled: true
      priority: 90
      prefix: "ecoitems"
      pdc-key: "ecoitems:item"

    mythicmobs:
      enabled: true
      priority: 90
      prefix: "mythicmobs"
      pdc-key: "mythicmobs:type"

    recipe-key:
      enabled: true
      priority: 80
      prefix: "recipe"

    custom-model-data:
      enabled: true
      priority: 50
      allow-at-syntax: true

    generic-pdc:
      enabled: true
      priority: 40
      prefix: "pdc"
      watched-keys:
        - "customcrafting:id"
        - "executableitems:id"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Workstations & Specialized Stations
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

stations:
  # Smelting Stations (Furnaces, Blast Furnaces, Smokers, Campfires)
  smelting:
    enabled: true
    restrict-furnace: true
    restrict-blast-furnace: true
    restrict-smoker: true
    restrict-campfire: true

    # Hopper protection: track player ownership of hoppers feeding into furnaces.
    # If true, automated hoppers inherit the placer's blueprint unlocks.
    # Unowned hoppers cannot smelt restricted recipes.
    track-hoppers: true

    # Play fail sound and smoke particles when a furnace smelt is blocked
    fail-effect: true

  # Stonecutter Station
  stonecutter:
    enabled: true
    # Display locked preview icons in the stonecutter result slot
    prepare-preview: true

  # Enchantment Table Station
  enchanting-table:
    enabled: true
    # Cancel the enchantment if the player lacks the blueprint for any applied enchantment
    cancel-if-locked: true
    # Notify the player in chat explaining which blueprint is missing
    send-fail-message: true

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Recipe Restrictions & Whitelist Mode
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

restrictions:
  # Operational mode:
  # - 'restricted-only': Whitelist mode where ALL standard Minecraft items and recipes
  #   are freely craftable by everyone by default!
  #   ONLY items matching 'restricted-items' require a blueprint. (Recommended for SMP).
  # - 'all': Universal progression mode where EVERY craftable item requires a blueprint.
  mode: "restricted-only"

  # List of items, materials, potions, or enchantments that require blueprints.
  # Supports exact names, wildcards (*), regular expressions (.*),
  # and optional category prefixes (craft:, potion:, enchant:).
  restricted-items:
    - "diamond_.*"
    - "netherite_.*"
    - "enchanted_golden_apple"
    - "beacon"
    - "potion:strength.*"
    - "potion:speed.*"
    - "enchantment:mending"
    - "enchantment:sharpness.*"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# User Experience & Client Previews (UX)
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

ux:
  vanilla-recipe-book:
    # Synchronize unlocked recipes with the player's vanilla Recipe Book upon joining
    sync-on-join: true
    # Synchronize incrementally when blueprints are unlocked, expire, or groups change
    sync-on-unlock-expire: true
    # If true, hides locked recipes from the green Recipe Book; if false, only warns on preview
    hide-locked-recipes: true

  prepare-preview:
    # Show clear locked feedback in Crafting, Smithing, and Anvil result slots
    enabled: true
    # Available modes:
    # - 'HIDE_RESULT': Clears the output slot when locked
    # - 'LOCKED_OVERLAY' (alias 'LOCKED_LORE'): Keeps original item icon with locked name/lore warning
    # - 'CUSTOM_ITEM' (alias 'BARRIER_ICON'): Shows the configured locked-item below
    mode: "LOCKED_OVERLAY"
    locked-item:
      material: BARRIER
      custom-model-data: 4001
      name: "<red><bold>Recipe Locked</bold></red>"
      lore:
        - "<gray>Required Blueprint:</gray> <yellow>{blueprint_name}</yellow>"
        - "<gray>Run</gray> <aqua>/cb info {blueprint_name}</aqua> <gray>to view details.</gray>"

docs.title: item-ownership
docs.text:
• Default: true
  • Operational Purpose: Prevents exploit trading. When true, physical blueprint items (FILLED_MAP, PAPER, etc.) have the recipient's UUID permanently stamped into their Persistent Data Container (PDC). Only the bound player can hold, inspect, and right-click to memorize the blueprint. If set to false, blueprints become tradeable commodities that players can sell, drop, or share across player factions.

docs.title: images-on-maps
docs.text:
• Default: true
  • Operational Purpose: Activates the native 128x128 map compositing engine. When true, any blueprint using item.material: FILLED_MAP renders a high-resolution drafting schematic featuring background textures, Guilloche corner frames, workstation badges, and item sprites. If disabled, blueprints render as standard vanilla maps.

docs.title: op-bypass
docs.text:
• Default: true
  • Gotcha: If you are testing recipe locks while having /op status, the plugin will allow you to craft the locked item freely! To test properly as an unauthorized player, either run /deop <your_name> or temporarily set op-bypass: false.

docs.title: 2. Multi-Server File Management (file-management)
docs.text:
The Golden Rule of Multi-Server Networks

On networks connected to a shared MySQL database, set sync-from-files: true strictly on ONE Primary Management Node (e.g. Lobby or Admin server). On all Worker Nodes (Survival, Skyblock, Factions), set sync-from-files: false.

  • sync-from-files: true (Primary Node): Recursively parses local YAML files in blueprints/, inserts/updates them in the shared database, safely prunes deleted blueprints (prune-deleted: true), and emits a real-time signal ping (cb_sync_signals) alerting worker nodes.
  • sync-from-files: false (Worker Nodes): Loads all blueprints directly from the shared MySQL database into memory. Worker nodes never overwrite the database with local files, eliminating race conditions.
  • auto-reload.debounce-delay-ms: Sets the delay (default: 1500ms) to wait before hot-reloading after a file is saved on disk, ensuring editors finish writing multi-byte files.

docs.title: 3. Redstone Crafter Interception (crafter)
docs.text:
• block-restricted: true: In Minecraft 1.21+, redstone-powered Crafter blocks (Material.CRAFTER) craft automatically without player clicks. When this setting is true, any attempt by an automated Crafter to produce a recipe restricted in restrictions.restricted-items is immediately intercepted and blocked.
  • fail-effect: true: When blocked, plays the dispenser fail sound (Sound.BLOCK_DISPENSER_FAIL) and spawns smoke particles at the Crafter's coordinates, signaling that the automated process is locked.
  • If set to block-restricted: false, Crafters bypass all blueprint checks, allowing redstone factories to mass-produce locked items.

docs.title: 4. Custom Item Identification (item-matching)
docs.text:
Modern RPG servers use custom item frameworks where hundreds of custom weapons share the base vanilla material DIAMOND_SWORD. The item-matching SPI inspects items in order of priority:

  1. itemsadder (ia:<namespace:id>): Hooks into ItemsAdder custom stacks.
  2. nexo (nexo:<id>): Hooks into Nexo custom items.
  3. oraxen (oraxen:<id>): Hooks into Oraxen custom items.
  4. mmoitems (mmoitems:<TYPE>:<ID>): Hooks into MMOItems equipment.
  5. ecoitems (ecoitems:<id>): Reads native Paper PDC key ecoitems:item.
  6. mythicmobs (mythicmobs:<id>): Reads native Paper PDC key mythicmobs:type.
  7. recipe-key (recipe:<namespace>:<key>): Matches custom datapack recipes.
  8. custom-model-data: Matches by CustomModelData integers.

docs.title: fallback-to-vanilla: true (Economy Safety Net)
docs.text: When true, if a custom sword (e.g. ia:weapons:flame_blade) does not have its own explicit custom blueprint, but the base material (DIAMOND_SWORD) is restricted, the player must unlock the base Diamond Sword blueprint to craft it. This prevents players from bypassing progression by crafting custom variants.

docs.title: 5. Workstations & Stations (stations)
docs.text:
• smelting.track-hoppers: true: Tracks the UUID of the player who placed hoppers feeding into smelting stations (Furnaces, Blast Furnaces, Smokers). Smelting only processes restricted recipes if the placing player owns the corresponding blueprint. Unowned or natural hoppers cannot smelt restricted items.
  • enchanting-table.cancel-if-locked: true: Prevents players from applying high-tier enchantments (such as Mending or Sharpness V) at an Enchantment Table unless they have unlocked the blueprint.

docs.title: ux.vanilla-recipe-book
docs.text:
• sync-on-join & sync-on-unlock-expire: Automatically synchronizes the green vanilla Recipe Book with the player's unlocked blueprints.
  • hide-locked-recipes: true: Removes locked recipes from the client Recipe Book so players only see recipes they are certified to craft.

docs.title: ux.prepare-preview
docs.text: Controls what appears in the crafting result slot when an unauthorized player arranges ingredients for a locked recipe: * HIDE_RESULT: The output slot is completely empty. * LOCKED_OVERLAY: Keeps the output item icon, but appends warning lore explaining that the recipe is locked. * CUSTOM_ITEM: Replaces the output slot with the item defined in locked-item (e.g., a red Barrier block with custom model data).

docs.title: Messages, Colors & MiniMessage Localization
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints features a modern Kyori MiniMessage localization engine (me.xztotal.plugins.craftingblueprints.i18n), replacing legacy section sign (§) color codes with rich, component-based formatting, true 24-bit RGB hex colors, multi-stop gradients, and dynamic context placeholders.

docs.title: Language Configuration & Hot-Reloading
docs.text:
The plugin ships with two canonical language files in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/:

  • messages_en.yml (English)
  • messages_es.yml (Spanish - canonical primary)

To reload your language files after editing without restarting your server, execute:

/cb reload lang

Automatic Per-Player Locale Resolution

On Paper servers, CraftingBlueprints automatically detects the Minecraft client language of each connecting player (player.locale()). A Spanish player automatically receives Spanish feedback from messages_es.yml, while an English player receives English feedback from messages_en.yml. If a player's client language is not installed, the plugin falls back to defaultLocaleRef.
