docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
docs.text: Direct, authoritative answers to the most common questions asked by server administrators and creators.

docs.title: Does CraftingBlueprints impact server TPS or cause lag spikes?
docs.text: No. CraftingBlueprints is engineered from the ground up for high-concurrency production networks: * All database persistence, HikariCP connection queries, file watching, and map graphic dithering execute strictly on asynchronous background threads. * Pre-quantized byte[16384] palette buffers are blitted onto maps in < 0.02 milliseconds per tick. * The main server thread is only consulted for instant Bukkit crafting event decisions, maintaining a solid 20.0 TPS.

docs.title: Can players exploit Shift-Clicking to bypass limited-use blueprints?
docs.text: No. CraftingBlueprints features an atomic Capacity Math Engine (ShiftCraftMath.kt). When a player shift-clicks a crafting table, the engine calculates the minimum between available ingredients, empty inventory space, and remaining blueprint uses: $$\text{CraftCount} = \min(\text{MatrixCapacity}, \text{InventorySpace}, \text{RemainingUses})$$ A player with 2 uses remaining who shift-clicks a full stack of materials will craft exactly 2 items, decrement exactly 2 uses, and leave the remaining materials untouched in the crafting grid.

docs.title: How do I prevent operators from bypassing recipe restrictions during testing?
docs.text: By default, op-bypass: true in config.yml allows server operators (/op) to craft, brew, and enchant all restricted recipes freely. * To test restrictions properly as a normal player, either deop yourself: /deop <your_name> * Or temporarily set op-bypass: false in config.yml and execute /cb reload config.

docs.title: What happens if a player's inventory is full when receiving a blueprint?
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints enforces Physical Overflow Preservation. When running /cb give, if the player's inventory has no free slots, the remaining blueprint items automatically drop onto the ground directly at the player's feet (world.dropItem(...)). No items ever vanish into the void.

docs.title: Does CraftingBlueprints work with custom items from ItemsAdder, Oraxen, and Nexo?
docs.text: Yes. The plugin features an extensible ItemIdentifierProvider SPI. You can gate custom weapons, armor, and tools using their native prefixes: * ItemsAdder: ia:<namespace:id> * Oraxen: oraxen:<id> * Nexo: nexo:<id> * MMOItems: mmoitems:<TYPE>:<ID> * Pure CustomModelData: diamond_sword@custom_model_data:1042 See our Custom Items Guide.

docs.title: Can I connect multiple servers to a shared MySQL database?
docs.text: Yes. CraftingBlueprints fully supports BungeeCord and Velocity networks. Follow the Golden Rule of Multi-Server Networks: * Designate ONE Primary Management Node (e.g. Hub) with sync-from-files: true. * Configure ALL Worker Nodes (Survival, Skyblock, Factions) with sync-from-files: false. When the master server reloads, it emits an atomic heartbeat ping (cb_sync_signals), and worker nodes automatically refresh their local cache within seconds. See our Multi-Server Setup Guide.

docs.title: How do I prevent Minecraft 1.21 redstone Crafters from bypassing blueprints?
docs.text: In config.yml, ensure crafter.block-restricted: true is enabled. When active, redstone-powered Crafter blocks attempting to produce restricted recipes are intercepted, emit dispenser fail clicks and smoke particles, and leave all raw materials safely in the grid.

docs.title: Do I need to restart my server when editing blueprint YAML files?
docs.text:
No. You can hot-reload your blueprints at any time with zero downtime using: 

/cb reload blueprints
If file-management.auto-reload.enabled: true is active, the plugin detects file saves on disk and hot-reloads automatically after a short 1.5-second debounce window.

docs.title: Reporting Bugs & Getting Help
docs.text: If you encounter unexpected behavior, suspect a bug, or have a feature proposal for CraftingBlueprints, follow this guide to report issues and receive prompt technical assistance.

docs.title: 1. Pre-Flight Checklist
docs.text:
Before opening an issue or asking for support, run through this quick checklist:

  • [ ] Verify Server Engine: Ensure you are running an official build of Paper or Purpur (1.18.2 – 1.21.x). CraftBukkit and standalone Spigot are not supported.
  • [ ] Verify Java Version: Minecraft 1.18.2–1.20.4 requires Java 17 or 21. Minecraft 1.20.5+ and 1.21+ strictly require Java 21.
  • [ ] Run Dry-Run Validation: Execute /cb validate to rule out syntax typos or malformed YAML indentation.
  • [ ] Capture /cb status: Run /cb status in console to inspect your active database backend, NMS adapter, and registered blueprint counts.
  • [ ] Check Server Logs: Search logs/latest.log for any relevant stack traces or warning banners.

docs.title: 2. Opening an Issue on GitHub
docs.text:
We track all official bug reports and feature requests through our GitHub repository:

  • Submit a Bug Report

    Report unexpected behavior, crafting desyncs, or plugin errors using our structured template.

  • Submit a Feature Request

    Propose new workstation integrations, map visual themes, or administrative quality-of-life tools.

docs.title: 3. What Information to Include
docs.text:
When submitting a ticket, always provide the following technical details:

  1. Exact Server Software & Build Number: (e.g. Purpur 1.20.4 build 2174).
  2. CraftingBlueprints Diagnostic Report: Paste the full output of /cb status.
  3. Database Backend: Whether your server is running on embedded sqlite or multi-server mysql.
  4. Console Logs: Upload your full logs/latest.log to a clean paste service such as mclo.gs or hastebin. Never post cropped screenshots of console text.
  5. Clear Step-by-Step Reproduction: Detailed numbered steps explaining how to trigger the issue on a clean test server.
  6. Relevant Configuration Snippets: The exact YAML block from config.yml or your blueprint file in blueprints/.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Common Issues
docs.text: This guide provides structured, step-by-step diagnostic workflows for resolving the most frequent operational challenges encountered by server administrators.

docs.title: 1. Issue: "Maps appear completely blank or show terrain"
docs.text: If blueprint items given to players appear as blank gray maps or show vanilla terrain maps instead of custom schematics:

docs.title: Diagnostic Checklist:
docs.text:
1. Verify Master Config: Open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml and verify: 
    images-on-maps: true
    If set to false, maps will not render custom graphics.
  2. Verify Custom PNG Dimensions & Format: If using custom images:
  3. The file must reside in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/images/backgrounds/.
  4. The image must be exactly 128 x 128 pixels. Any other dimensions will fail to load or be rejected.
  5. The file must be 32-bit RGBA PNG format. Progressive JPEGs, animated GIFs, and WebP formats are not supported.
  6. Verify Cross-Server Map Re-Linking: If this occurs when players transfer from another server on a BungeeCord/Velocity network:
  7. Verify that the Primary Node has sync-from-files: true and all Worker Nodes have sync-from-files: false.
  8. Ensure that all sub-servers are connected to the exact same MySQL database.
  9. CraftingBlueprints' MapRelinkListener will automatically intercept the item and bind it to the local server's canonical Map ID in-place upon inventory open.
  10. Reload Map System: Execute: 
    /cb reload all

docs.title: 2. Issue: "Players can craft items without unlocking blueprints"
docs.text: If players are able to craft recipes that you intended to lock:

docs.title: Diagnostic Checklist:
docs.text:
1. Check for Operator Bypass (op-bypass): Are you testing with a player account that has /op status? By default, op-bypass: true in config.yml allows all server operators to craft, brew, and enchant restricted recipes freely.
  2. Fix: Temporarily deop your account: /deop <your_player_name> or set op-bypass: false in config.yml and run /cb reload config.
  3. Check your Restriction Mode: In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:
  4. If restrictions.mode: "restricted-only", recipes are only locked if they match an entry in restricted-items. Unlisted recipes are completely free for all players by default!
  5. Verify that your target item pattern (e.g. diamond_.*, netherite_.*, beacon) is explicitly listed under restricted-items.
  6. Check Permission Group Grants: Run /lp user <player> permission check craftingblueprints.group.<id> to ensure the player has not been granted a permission group that already unlocks that recipe category.

docs.title: 3. Issue: "YAML syntax errors or failed reloads"
docs.text: If the server console reports an error when loading blueprint files:

docs.title: Diagnostic Checklist:
docs.text:
1. Run Dry-Run Validation: In console or in-game, execute: 
    /cb validate
  2. Review the Diagnostic Output: The validator reports:
  3. The exact file path and line number of the error.
  4. Indentation errors (remember: YAML strictly prohibits tab characters; always use standard spaces).
  5. Typo suggestions via Levenshtein distance (e.g. roseta $\rightarrow$ rosette).
  6. Rest Assured with Atomic Fail-Safe: If a YAML file has a syntax error, CraftingBlueprints triggers an atomic abort. Zero database records are modified, zero blueprints are pruned, and your live server continues running with the previous valid configuration until you fix the typo!

docs.title: 4. Issue: "Preset or Scaffolder rejected on Worker Node"
docs.text:
If executing /cb preset apply or /cb generate results in an error: 

[CraftingBlueprints] Command rejected: This server is configured as a Worker Node (sync-from-files: false).

docs.title: Cause & Solution:
docs.text: To prevent database divergence and split-brain conflicts across multi-server MySQL networks, all file generation and preset deployments must be executed on your designated Primary Management Node (sync-from-files: true). * Connect to your Hub or Lobby server and execute the command there. * The master server will update the shared database and broadcast an atomic sync signal (cb_sync_signals) to all worker nodes automatically.

docs.title: 5. Issue: "Minecraft 1.21 Crafters continue auto-crafting locked recipes"
docs.text: If automated redstone Crafter blocks are mass-producing restricted recipes:

docs.title: Diagnostic Checklist:
docs.text:
1. Open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml.
  2. Verify that the Crafter interception block is configured: 
    crafter:
  block-restricted: true
  fail-effect: true
  3. Run /cb reload config.
  4. Ensure the item being produced matches your restrictions.restricted-items list.

docs.title: Installation & System Requirements
docs.text: This guide provides the system prerequisites, compatibility matrix, and a clean 4-step installation procedure for deploying CraftingBlueprints on modern Minecraft servers.

docs.title: System Requirements & Compatibility
docs.text:
CraftingBlueprints is engineered specifically for modern Paper-based server software. It features automated version adapters that load dynamically depending on your server runtime. A single .jar file supports all listed versions.

Requirement Supported Versions Operational Notes Server Engine Paper, Purpur (1.18.2 – 1.21.x) Modern Paper forks are required. Legacy CraftBukkit and standalone Spigot are not supported due to missing Adventure and PDC APIs. Java Runtime Java 17 or Java 21+ Minecraft 1.18.2–1.20.4 runs on Java 17 or 21. Minecraft 1.20.5+ and 1.21+ strictly require Java 21 minimum. Database SQLite (Default) or MySQL 8.0+ / MariaDB 10.5+ Standalone servers run on embedded SQLite with zero setup. Multi-server networks connect to MySQL via built-in HikariCP connection pooling. Network Proxies Velocity, BungeeCord, Waterfall Full support for cross-server networks via shared MySQL and real-time heartbeat sync signals.

Automated Version Abstraction Layer

CraftingBlueprints uses an internal Version Abstraction Layer. You do not need separate builds for 1.18.2, 1.20.4, or 1.21.x. Advanced features (such as 1.21 Crafter block interception or 1.20 3-slot Smithing Tables) activate automatically when running on compatible server versions and remain safely dormant on older versions.

docs.title: Clean Installation in 4 Steps
docs.text:
Paper / Purpur (Single Server)Multi-Server Network (Bungee / Velocity)
  1. Download the Plugin: Obtain the latest official CraftingBlueprints-x.x.x.jar.
  2. Place in Plugins Directory: Copy the .jar directly into your server's plugins/ directory: 
    your-server/
└── plugins/
    └── CraftingBlueprints-x.x.x.jar
  3. Start the Server: Start the server to generate default configuration files, bundled templates, and sample blueprints. !!! warning "Avoid /reload" Never use the Bukkit /reload or /reload confirm command when installing or updating plugins. A clean restart ensures that database connection pools, file watchers, and version adapters initialize safely.
  4. Verify Boot Output: Review your server console for the startup diagnostics banner: 
    [CraftingBlueprints] Enabling CraftingBlueprints vX.X.X...
[CraftingBlueprints] Detected Server Engine: Paper 1.20.4 (Adapter: Adapter_v1_20_R3)
[CraftingBlueprints] SQLite database connection established: plugins/CraftingBlueprints/crafting_blueprints.db
[CraftingBlueprints] Loaded 3 blueprint groups: default (142 recipes), vip (157 recipes), pro (210 recipes).
[CraftingBlueprints] Successfully registered 42 blueprints from YAML files.
  1. Install on Every Server: Copy CraftingBlueprints-x.x.x.jar into the plugins/ directory of each sub-server (Hub, Survival, Skyblock, etc.).
  2. Configure Central MySQL: On every server, open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml and set database-type: mysql with your shared database credentials.
  3. Enforce the Golden Rule:
  4. Designate one Primary Management Server (e.g., Hub/Admin) with: 
    file-management:
  sync-from-files: true
  5. Configure all Worker Servers (Survival, Skyblock, etc.) with: 
    file-management:
  sync-from-files: false
  6. Start Servers & Confirm Sync: Start the primary server first, then the worker nodes. Review our Multi-Server Setup Guide for network-specific connection pooling advice.

docs.title: First-Run Diagnostics (/cb status)
docs.text:
Once your server has fully started, verify the operational health of CraftingBlueprints by running the status diagnostic command in console or as a server operator:

/cb status

This diagnostic report provides immediate insight into your deployment:

  • Engine & Version Adapter: Confirms the active Paper version and corresponding capability adapter (Smithing Table 3-slot, Data Components, Crafter block).
  • Database Backend: Displays active connection status (SQLite (Connected) or MySQL (HikariCP Active)), active connection pool statistics, and round-trip query latency.
  • Blueprint Counts: Reports the total number of blueprints registered across all categories (singles, packages, mysteries).
  • File Management Mode: Shows whether the node is running as a Master Node (sync-from-files: true) or a Worker Node (sync-from-files: false).
  • Memory & Buffer Cache: Displays active memory consumption for player profiles, blueprint definitions, and pre-quantized map byte buffers.

docs.title: Recommended Complementary Plugins
docs.text:
While CraftingBlueprints works completely standalone with vanilla Minecraft economies, it integrates seamlessly with industry-standard server plugins:

  • Vault + Economy Provider (EssentialsX, Economy): Enables buying and selling blueprints directly through the /cb item list catalog GUI.
  • LuckPerms: The recommended permissions plugin for managing player progression tiers and recipe groups (craftingblueprints.group.<id>). See our LuckPerms Guide.
  • PlaceholderAPI: Allows surfacing remaining blueprint uses, active unlock counts, and expiration timers in scoreboards, tablists, and chat formats.
  • Custom Item Plugins: Full support for custom weapons, tools, and armor from ItemsAdder, Oraxen, Nexo, MMOItems, EcoItems, and MythicMobs.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Now that CraftingBlueprints is installed and healthy, test your first custom blueprint in under 3 minutes with our Quickstart Guide.

docs.title: Quickstart: Your First Blueprint in 3 Minutes
docs.text: This hands-on walkthrough guides you through creating, testing, granting, and crafting your very first custom blueprint on a live server.

docs.title: 1. Create a Test Blueprint File
docs.text:
Navigate to your server directory and create a new YAML file named obsidian_blade.yml inside the blueprints/ directory:

plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/obsidian_blade.yml

Paste the following production-ready configuration:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  obsidian_blade:
    # 1. Target Minecraft recipe to unlock
    blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD
    name: "<gradient:#9900EE:#FF0055><bold>Obsidian Blade Blueprint</bold></gradient>"

    # 2. Durability & Limits (permanent = unlocked forever)
    permanent: true
    time: 0
    uses: 0

    # 3. Economy Pricing (Requires Vault)
    price: 5000.0
    sell_price: 1250.0

    # 4. In-Game Physical Item Representation
    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    # 5. Visual Map Drafting Aesthetic
    map:
      theme: forge              # Volcanic basalt & ember background
      frame: rosette            # Regal gilded corner rosettes
      badge: smithing           # Workstation icon on top-left
      icon_scale: 2             # Sharp 2x pixel-art scaling
      drop_shadow: true         # Soft ambient item shadow

    # 6. MiniMessage Lore Description
    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{blueprint_name}</white>"
      - "<gray>Status:</gray> <green>Permanent Unlock</green>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Shop Value:</yellow> <gold>${price}</gold>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Hold this map and Right-Click to memorize the schematic.</dark_gray>"

docs.title: 2. Dry-Run Syntax Validation (/cb validate)
docs.text:
Before reloading your live server, execute the dry-run validator command in your server console or in-game:

/cb validate

CraftingBlueprints parses all YAML files in blueprints/ and verifies: * All Bukkit materials and recipe identifiers are valid on your server version. * Map themes, frames, and badge identifiers conform to the visual rendering engine. * YAML indentation and structure are completely error-free.

If everything is valid, the console displays: 

[CraftingBlueprints] Validation passed: 1 blueprint file verified with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

docs.title: 3. Hot-Reload the Blueprints
docs.text:
Apply your new file to the live server with zero downtime and zero lag:

/cb reload blueprints

You will see immediate console confirmation that obsidian_blade.yml was parsed, synchronized to the database, and registered in runtime memory.

Automatic File Watcher

If file-management.auto-reload.enabled: true is active in config.yml, you do not even need to type /cb reload blueprints. The plugin detects file saves on disk and hot-reloads automatically after a short 1.5-second debounce window.

docs.title: 4. Grant the Blueprint Item to Yourself
docs.text:
Give yourself the blueprint using the /cb give command:

/cb give <your_player_name> obsidian_blade 1

Look at your hotbar. You will receive a high-resolution in-game map (Material.FILLED_MAP) rendering the volcanic Dwarven Forge theme, the central Diamond Sword sprite, the Smithing Table workstation badge, and the Guilloche corner rosettes.

Overflow Safety Guarantee

If your inventory happens to be completely full when running /cb give, CraftingBlueprints automatically drops the leftover items safely onto the ground directly at your feet, preventing silent item deletion.

docs.title: 5. Unlock and Craft in Survival
docs.text:
1. Memorize the Blueprint: Place the map in your main hand and Right-Click. A sound effect plays and chat confirms: 
    [CraftingBlueprints] You have unlocked the blueprint for Obsidian Blade Blueprint!
    The physical map is consumed from your hand.
  2. Open a Crafting Table: Place two diamonds and a stick into the 3x3 crafting matrix. The Diamond Sword appears in the result slot and crafts normally.
  3. Test Whitelist Protection:
  4. Open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml and ensure restrictions.mode: "restricted-only" with diamond_.* included in restricted-items.
  5. Either temporarily deop yourself (/deop <your_name>) or set op-bypass: false in config.yml.
  6. Have an unauthorized player (or test account) place the same ingredients into the crafting table: the recipe will be locked, and the player will be notified that they lack the required blueprint!

docs.title: Server Blueprint Catalog (/cb item list)
docs.text: The server blueprint catalog (/cb item list) provides players with an interactive, paginated encyclopedia of every crafting blueprint available on the server.

docs.title: Opening the Catalog
docs.text:
To open the catalog in-game:

/cb item list

Permission Required: craftingblueprints.item.list (Granted to all players by default).

docs.title: 1. Paginated Windowing & Audio Feedback
docs.text:
• Smooth Pagination: Clicking the navigation arrows shifts through pages seamlessly with page-turn audio feedback (playPageTurnSound()).
  • Database-Windowed Pagination: On networks with hundreds of blueprints, the catalog queries database pages incrementally without loading unneeded items into memory, ensuring zero tick drops.

docs.title: 2. Status Indicators & Badges
docs.text:
Each blueprint item displayed in the catalog shows an intuitive status indicator:

  • Unlocked: The player has learned this recipe and can craft it freely.
  • Locked: The player has not yet unlocked this recipe. Hovering displays the purchase price or acquisition hint.
  • Expiring: The recipe is currently active with limited uses or a countdown timer.
  • [⚡ Archivo] File-Managed: Displayed for server administrators indicating the blueprint is declared in YAML files on disk.

docs.title: 3. One-Click Vault Economy Purchase
docs.text: If Vault is installed and the blueprint declares a price: field: * The item lore displays: <yellow>Catalog Price:</yellow> <green>${price}</green>. * Left-Clicking a locked blueprint prompts a purchase confirmation dialogue. * If the player has sufficient balance: 1. Vault deducts the cost from the player's account. 2. The blueprint is unlocked immediately. 3. A celebration sound plays, and the status icon transitions from to .

docs.title: 4. Interactive 3x3 Recipe Inspector
docs.text:
• Right-Clicking any blueprint in the catalog opens an expanded inspection card:
  • Renders the exact 3x3 crafting matrix, smithing template arrangement, or brewing stand ingredients.
  • Displays required materials, output item yields, and lore descriptions.

docs.title: The Return Navigation Stack (/cb return)
docs.text:
CraftingBlueprints maintains an in-memory LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) navigation stack per player session via MenuSessionManager:

  • When a player navigates from the personal dashboard (/cb menu) into the catalog (/cb item list), and then into a detailed recipe inspection view:
  • Clicking the Back button or typing /cb return pops the last menu and re-opens the catalog on the exact page they were browsing.
  • Typing /cb return again returns them to their personal dashboard.
  • ESC Exit Context Preservation: If a player accidentally closes a menu by pressing the ESC key, lastClosedMenu remembers their active context. Running /cb return instantly restores the interface right where they left off.

docs.title: In-Game Blueprint Editor (/cb item edit)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints allows server administrators to inspect and modify blueprint settings visually from inside the game without accessing server files or rebooting the instance.

docs.title: Opening the Visual Editor
docs.text:
To open the interactive editor for a specific blueprint:

/cb item edit <blueprint_id>

Permission Required: craftingblueprints.item.edit (Default: op).

docs.title: File-Managed Immutability ([⚡ Archivo])
docs.text:
To prevent accidental configuration desynchronization on servers using Git workflows and declarative YAML files:

  • File-Managed Blueprints (is_file_managed: true):
  • Blueprints loaded from .yml files in blueprints/ display a prominent [⚡ Archivo] badge in the interface.
  • These blueprints are read-only and immutable from in-game commands and menus.

  • If an operator attempts to modify a file-managed blueprint in-game, the interface notifies them to edit the source .yml file directly on disk, preserving Git version control integrity.

  • In-Game Manual Blueprints (is_file_managed: false):

  • Blueprints created in-game via commands or modifier menus are fully editable.
  • All adjustments are persisted directly to the database and automatically exported to exports/manual_blueprints.yml.

• Prompts the administrator in chat to enter new display names or lore lines.
  • Full support for MiniMessage gradient tags (<gradient:#HEX1:#HEX2>) and context placeholders ({player}, {uses}, {time}, {price}).

docs.title: Package & Mystery Modifier Menus
docs.text:
For multi-recipe packages (PackageModifierMenu) and mystery roll crates (MysteryModifierMenu):

  • Anti-Duplicate Invariant: When adding blueprints from the operator's bottom inventory into a package or mystery container, the system verifies that no item with the identical blueprint ID is already present. Duplicate additions are rejected with error audio feedback.
  • Weight Configuration (MysteryElementModifierMenu): Operators can click on any reward in a mystery crate to adjust its relative probability weight (weight: 1..100). The interface automatically displays the percentage roll probability in real time.
  • Type Safety Guard: Mystery blueprints cannot be nested inside other mystery blueprints, preventing infinite roll recursion and serialization corruption.

docs.title: Automatic Exporter & Rolling Backups
docs.text:
Whenever in-game blueprints are saved: 1. The updated definition is persisted to the database. 2. The export engine automatically dumps all in-game blueprints into: 

plugins/CraftingBlueprints/exports/manual_blueprints.yml
3. Periodic rolling backups are created automatically in: 
plugins/CraftingBlueprints/exports/backups/manual_blueprints_<timestamp>.yml
4. If you later declare the same blueprint ID in a file inside blueprints/, the plugin adopts the YAML definition, sets is_file_managed: true, and removes it from the manual export dump.

docs.title: 4. Navigation Stack & Return Button (/cb return)

docs.title: Anti-Steal Item Protection & Inventory Security
docs.text:
All menus in CraftingBlueprints inherit from BaseMenu.kt and are protected by an automated, low-level anti-steal security engine:

  • Slot Locking: Non-input menu slots are locked. Shift-clicking, dragging, hotkey swapping, and dropping items out of the interface are intercepted and cancelled immediately.
  • PDC Menu Tagging: All visual icons placed inside menus are tagged with a Persistent Data Container marker (ItemPDT(ItemManager.MENU_TYPE)).
  • Purge Engine: If a player attempts to exploit client-side glitches, disconnect macros, or death drops to extract GUI items, the ItemInteractListener intercepts the item on cursor, hotbar, pickup, block placement, or death, and instantly purges the phantom item.
  • Zero menu items can ever leak into the server's survival economy.

docs.title: Automated Crafter Interception (Minecraft 1.21+)
docs.text:
Minecraft 1.21 introduced the redstone-powered Crafter block (Material.CRAFTER), enabling automated, hopper-driven crafting without a human player clicking an inventory slot.

Because Crafters operate autonomously when pulsed with redstone, they do not trigger standard player crafting events (CraftItemEvent). Without dedicated protection, players can build automated redstone factories to mass-produce locked, rare, epic, or mythic items (such as Netherite equipment or beacons) without ever finding or unlocking the required blueprints, completely circumventing your server's progression economy.

CraftingBlueprints features native, low-level interception to protect your economy from this exploit.

docs.title: How Protection Works
docs.text:
When a redstone pulse activates a Crafter block:

  1. Recipe Inspection: The plugin intercepts the pending craft before items are produced, resolving the output item and recipe key.
  2. Restriction Engine Consultation: The plugin queries RestrictionEngine.isBlueprintRequired(name, type):
  3. Unrestricted Recipes: If the recipe does not require a blueprint (e.g. iron ingots into blocks, bread, paper, or torches in Whitelist Mode), the craft executes normally with zero interference.
  4. Restricted Recipes: If the item requires a blueprint, the Crafter evaluates the active configuration policy.
  5. Execution Policy Enforcement:
  6. Blocked: The craft is cancelled. The Crafter block emits fail particles and sounds, and all ingredient items remain safely inside the Crafter's grid without duplication or item loss.
  7. Bypassed: If configured by the administrator, the Crafter is allowed to produce the locked recipe autonomously.

docs.title: Configuration in config.yml
docs.text:
Configure the interception behavior in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Automated Crafter Interception (Minecraft 1.21+)
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

crafter:
  # If true, redstone-powered Crafter blocks are blocked from crafting
  # recipes that require an unlocked blueprint.
  # If false, Crafters bypass player checks and craft all recipes automatically.
  block-restricted: true

  # If true, plays a dispenser fail click sound and spawns smoke particles
  # at the Crafter block when a craft is blocked.
  fail-effect: true

docs.title: Operating Policies: Block vs Bypass
docs.text:
Block Policy (block-restricted: true) - RECOMMENDEDBypass Policy (block-restricted: false)
  • Economic Integrity Guarantee: Autonomous machines cannot craft recipes that players haven't earned.
  • No Resource Deletion: When a Crafter block receives a redstone pulse while loaded with ingredients for a locked recipe, the craft is cancelled cleanly. The raw materials remain inside the Crafter's 9 slots.
  • Visual & Audio Feedback: If fail-effect: true is enabled, the Crafter emits the classic dispenser fail click (Sound.BLOCK_DISPENSER_FAIL) and puffs of smoke particles (Particle.SMOKE_NORMAL), alerting nearby players that the automated recipe is locked.
  • Recommended For: Survival SMP, RPG networks, Skyblock, and balanced economies.
  • Full Redstone Automation: Allows automated Crafter machines to produce all recipes freely, even if players would normally need a blueprint to craft them manually.
  • Use Case: Anarchy servers or specialized technical modded networks where redstone automation is intentionally unrestricted.

docs.title: Multi-Version Compatibility
docs.text: Because CrafterCraftEvent only exists in Bukkit/Paper API 1.21+: * On servers running Paper 1.18.2 or 1.20.4, this module loads as a lightweight no-op adapter (NoOpCrafterAdapter). It introduces zero performance overhead, executes zero listeners, and causes zero ClassNotFoundException errors. * On servers running Paper 1.21.1+, the dedicated implementation (CrafterAdapterImpl) activates automatically without configuration changes.

docs.title: Player Experience & Crafting Mechanics
docs.text: This guide explores the complete in-game player journey: how players acquire blueprints, inspect technical drafting maps, right-click to memorize schematics, and interact with crafting tables and workstations under active restriction policies.

docs.title: 1. Blueprint Acquisition
docs.text:
Players encounter blueprints through multiple gameplay avenues:

  • In-Game Economy Catalog: Purchasing blueprints for server currency via /cb item list or /cb buy.
  • Dungeon & World Loot: Discovered inside Bastion Remnants, End Cities, Nether Fortresses, and Ancient Cities.
  • Crate & Quest Rewards: Rewarded by quest plugins or loot crate keys.
  • Direct Administrative Grants: Granted by server operators or automated scripts via /cb give <player> <id> [amount].

Item Ownership Protection

When item-ownership: true is enabled in config.yml, physical blueprint items are permanently bound to the UUID of the recipient. If an unauthorized player attempts to hold, trade, or right-click the blueprint, an ownership warning is displayed and the unlock is blocked.

docs.title: 2. Inspecting and Memorizing Schematics
docs.text:
When a player receives a blueprint map (Material.FILLED_MAP):

  1. Visual Drafting Inspection: Holding the map in either hand renders a photorealistic 128x128 pixel drafting schematic featuring the workstation badge, the central item sprite, corner Guilloché rosettes, and remaining craft counts.
  2. Right-Click Memorization: The player holds the blueprint in their main hand and Right-Clicks:
  3. A clean chime sound effect plays (Sound.ENTITY_PLAYER_LEVELUP or configured sound).
  4. Swirling enchanting particles appear at the player's eye level.
  5. A localized chat notification confirms the unlock: 
    [CraftingBlueprints] You have unlocked the blueprint for Obsidian Blade Blueprint!
  6. The physical map item is consumed from the player's hand (unless configured otherwise).
  7. The recipe is registered permanently or temporally into the player's account database profile.

docs.title: 3. The Workbench & Crafting Experience
docs.text: Once a blueprint is unlocked, the player approaches any standard 3x3 Crafting Table:

docs.title: Scenario A: The Blueprint is Unlocked
docs.text:
• Placing ingredients into the matrix immediately generates the crafted output item.
  • The player can click to retrieve single items or Shift-Click to craft in bulk.
  • If the blueprint has limited uses (e.g. 5 crafts), each crafted item decrements the counter in real time. When the counter reaches zero, the recipe locks automatically.

docs.title: Scenario B: The Recipe is Restricted & Locked
docs.text:
If the player arranges ingredients for a locked recipe without owning the blueprint: * Result Slot Preview: Governed by ux.prepare-preview in config.yml: * HIDE_RESULT: The crafting table output slot remains completely empty. * LOCKED_OVERLAY: Keeps the output item icon, but appends red warning lore: <red><bold>Recipe Locked</bold></red>. * CUSTOM_ITEM: Renders a custom indicator (e.g. a red Barrier icon). * Click Interception: If the player attempts to click the locked output slot: * The craft is instantly cancelled. * An informative message is sent to chat explaining which blueprint is missing: 

[CraftingBlueprints] You must unlock the Ancient Netherite Battleaxe blueprint before crafting this item!
* Ingredients remain completely safe inside the 3x3 grid without duplication, corruption, or loss.

docs.title: 4. Vanilla Recipe Book Integration
docs.text:
Under ux.vanilla-recipe-book in config.yml:

ux:
  vanilla-recipe-book:
    sync-on-join: true
    sync-on-unlock-expire: true
    hide-locked-recipes: true
  • sync-on-join: true: When players log into the server, the plugin synchronizes their unlocked blueprints with their client-side green vanilla Recipe Book.
  • sync-on-unlock-expire: true: When a player unlocks a blueprint or an active timer expires, their Recipe Book updates instantly without requiring a re-log.
  • hide-locked-recipes: true: Hides locked recipes from the client Recipe Book, ensuring players only see items they are authorized to craft.

docs.title: 5. Shift-Craft Safety & Capacity Math
docs.text:
A frequent vulnerability in Minecraft progression plugins is shift-crafting: players place 64 stacks of ingredients into the matrix, shift-click once, and produce 64 items while the plugin only deducts 1 use from their counter.

CraftingBlueprints prevents this exploit via an atomic Capacity Math Engine (ShiftCraftMath.kt):

$$\text{ActualCrafts} = \min\left( \text{MatrixCapacity}, \; \text{InventorySpaceCapacity}, \; \text{RemainingUses} \right)$$

  1. Matrix Capacity: Determines how many items the ingredients can produce.
  2. Inventory Space Capacity: Evaluates the player's open inventory slots and partial stacks to determine how many items can be received without dropping onto the ground.
  3. Usage Capacity: Evaluates the remaining uses on the player's active blueprint.

docs.title: Real-World Example:
docs.text:
• A player with 2 remaining uses on a Netherite Sword scroll places materials for 8 swords into the table and shift-clicks.
  • The engine crafts exactly 2 swords.
  • Exactly 2 uses are consumed, locking the blueprint.
  • The remaining materials for 6 swords remain completely safe in the crafting matrix. Zero over-crafting is permitted.

docs.title: 6. Real-Time Recipe Inspection (/cb info)
docs.text:
Players can inspect any blueprint recipe directly in-game without opening web browsers:

/cb info <blueprint_id>

This opens an interactive inspection menu displaying: * The 3x3 crafting ingredient matrix or smithing ingredients. * Active durability mode (Permanent, Countdown Timer, or Remaining Uses). * Rarity tier, catalog purchase price, and item lore.

docs.title: Potions, Smithing Table & Specialized Workstations
docs.text: Beyond standard 3x3 crafting tables, CraftingBlueprints intercepts and gates specialized Minecraft workstations: Alchemy (Brewing Stands), Smithing Tables (Netherite Upgrades & Armor Trims), Smelting Furnaces, Stonecutters, and Enchantment Tables.

docs.title: 1. Gating Alchemy & Potion Brewing
docs.text: High-tier combat potions (Strength II, Speed II, Invisibility, Turtle Master) can destabilize PvP economies if left unrestricted. CraftingBlueprints tracks Brewing Stand operations in real time.

docs.title: Step 1: Restrict Potions in config.yml
docs.text:
Under restrictions.restricted-items, add potion patterns using the potion: category prefix:

restrictions:
  mode: "restricted-only"
  restricted-items:
    - "potion:strength.*"
    - "potion:speed.*"
    - "potion:invisibility.*"
    - "potion:turtle_master.*"

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Alchemy Blueprint
docs.text:
In any blueprint file (e.g. plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/alchemy.yml):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  elixir_of_strength:
    blueprint: STRENGTH
    name: "<gradient:#FF0000:#FF7700><bold>Elixir of Greater Strength Blueprint</bold></gradient>"
    permanent: true

    item:
      material: POTION
      glowing: true

    map:
      theme: transmutation_circle
      frame: runic
      badge: brewing

    lore:
      - "<gray>Classification:</gray> <gold>Master Alchemy</gold>"
      - "<gray>Unlocks:</gray> <white>Strength I & Strength II Brewing</white>"
      - ""
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click in hand to memorize the recipe.</dark_gray>"

docs.title: In-Game Brewing Interception:
docs.text:
1. When a player inserts ingredients and water bottles into a Brewing Stand, the plugin evaluates the output bottles upon brewing completion.
  2. If the player who loaded the stand has unlocked the blueprint, the brewing completes successfully.
  3. If the player lacks the blueprint, the brewing operation is blocked and ingredients remain safe.

docs.title: 2. Gating Smithing Table Upgrades (Netherite & Armor Trims)
docs.text: Minecraft 1.20+ introduced the 3-slot Smithing Table requiring a Smithing Template, a Base Item, and an Ingot/Crystal Addition.

docs.title: Restricting Netherite Upgrades
docs.text:
To prevent players from upgrading Diamond equipment into Netherite without finding ancient schematics:

In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

restrictions:
  mode: "restricted-only"
  restricted-items:
    - "netherite_sword"
    - "netherite_pickaxe"
    - "netherite_axe"
    - "netherite_shovel"
    - "netherite_hoe"
    - "netherite_helmet"
    - "netherite_chestplate"
    - "netherite_leggings"
    - "netherite_boots"

In your blueprint file (e.g. blueprints/netherite.yml):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  ancient_netherite_smithing:
    blueprint: NETHERITE_CHESTPLATE
    name: "<gradient:#FF5555:#FFAA00><bold>Ancient Netherite Smithing Technique</bold></gradient>"
    permanent: true

    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    map:
      theme: dwarven_magma
      frame: rosette
      badge: smithing
      item_outline:
        enabled: true
        width: 2
        color: "gold"

    lore:
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>Netherite Upgrades</white>"
      - "<gray>Status:</gray> <green>Permanent Unlock</green>"
      - ""
      - "<yellow>Grants knowledge to forge Netherite armor.</yellow>"

docs.title: In-Game Smithing Interception:
docs.text:
• When an unauthorized player inserts a Netherite Upgrade Template, a Diamond item, and a Netherite Ingot, the output slot remains locked.
  • If ux.prepare-preview.mode: "LOCKED_OVERLAY" is configured, the output slot displays the Netherite item with red warning lore: <red><bold>Recipe Locked: Requires Ancient Netherite Smithing Technique</bold></red>.

docs.title: 3. Workstations Configuration (stations)
docs.text:
Under stations: in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml, configure workstation enforcement:

stations:
  # Smelting Stations (Furnace, Blast Furnace, Smoker, Campfire)
  smelting:
    enabled: true
    restrict-furnace: true
    restrict-blast-furnace: true
    restrict-smoker: true
    restrict-campfire: true

    # Hopper Ownership Protection: tracks the player who placed the hopper.
    # Unowned hoppers cannot smelt restricted recipes.
    track-hoppers: true

    # Play fail click and smoke particles when a smelt is blocked
    fail-effect: true

  # Stonecutter Station
  stonecutter:
    enabled: true
    prepare-preview: true

  # Enchantment Table Station
  enchanting-table:
    enabled: true
    cancel-if-locked: true
    send-fail-message: true

docs.title: Hopper Protection for Automated Furnaces:
docs.text: When players automate smelting using hoppers feeding into Furnaces or Blast Furnaces: * When track-hoppers: true is enabled, CraftingBlueprints records the UUID of the player who placed the hopper into its PersistentDataContainer (PDC). * The smelting station inherits the placer's blueprint unlocks. * Hoppers placed by unauthorized players (or naturally generated hoppers) cannot automatically smelt restricted items.

docs.title: Recipe Restrictions (Whitelist Mode vs Universal Gating)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints features an intelligent restriction engine (RestrictionEngine.kt) allowing server administrators to choose between Selective Whitelist Mode (recommended for Survival SMP) and Universal Progression Mode (recommended for Hardcore RPG).

docs.title: Operating Modes Comparison
docs.text:
Configured in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml under the restrictions: block:

restrictions:
  # Mode options: 'restricted-only' or 'all'
  mode: "restricted-only"

  # Items, recipes, potions, or enchantments that require blueprints
  restricted-items:
    - "diamond_.*"
    - "netherite_.*"
    - "enchanted_golden_apple"
    - "beacon"
    - "potion:strength.*"
    - "potion:speed.*"
    - "enchantment:mending"
    - "enchantment:sharpness.*"
Selective Whitelist Mode (mode: 'restricted-only')Universal Progression Mode (mode: 'all')
  • Default for Modern SMP & Skyblock Servers.
  • All standard Minecraft recipes are completely FREE for all players by default! Players can craft wooden tools, stone pickaxes, iron armor, torches, furnaces, and beds without ever touching a blueprint.
  • ONLY items matching restricted-items require a blueprint.
  • Why choose this mode? It eliminates player frustration. You can introduce custom blueprints for endgame gear (such as Netherite weapons, Beacons, or Mending enchantments) while leaving standard survival crafting 100% natural and unhindered.
  • Designed for Hardcore RPG, Skyblock, and Quest Networks.
  • Every single craftable item, potion, and enchantment on your server requires a blueprint before it can be produced.
  • Players must discover, purchase, or unlock blueprints for basic wood, stone, iron, and farming equipment step-by-step.
  • Combine this mode with Permission Groups to grant tiers of basic recipes to player ranks automatically.

docs.title: Pattern Matching Reference Table
docs.text:
The restricted-items: list supports exact identifiers, wildcard globs, regular expressions (regex), and category prefixes:

Pattern Syntax Category Filtered Example Matches Operational Behavior beacon Crafting BEACON Exact material match. Case-insensitive. enchanted_golden_apple Crafting ENCHANTED_GOLDEN_APPLE Locks crafting of god apples (if enabled by datapacks). diamond_.* Crafting DIAMOND_SWORD, DIAMOND_CHESTPLATE, DIAMOND_PICKAXE, etc. Regex matching all equipment starting with diamond_. netherite_.* Crafting & Smithing NETHERITE_HELMET, NETHERITE_SWORD, NETHERITE_AXE, etc. Regex matching all Netherite tools, weapons, and armor. *gold* Crafting GOLDEN_SWORD, GOLDEN_APPLE, GOLD_INGOT, etc. Wildcard glob matching any item containing "gold". potion:strength.* Alchemy / Brewing Strength I, Strength II, Extended & Splash variants Locks brewing of all Strength potion variants. potion:speed.* Alchemy / Brewing Speed I, Speed II, Splash Speed Locks brewing of all Speed potion variants. enchantment:mending Anvil / Enchanting Mending books and items in anvils Locks combining or applying Mending enchantments. enchantment:sharpness.* Anvil / Enchanting Sharpness I through Sharpness V Locks applying Sharpness enchantments. smelt:iron_ingot Furnace / Smelting Raw iron $\rightarrow$ Iron ingot Locks smelting iron ingots in furnaces and blast furnaces. stonecut:.*stairs Stonecutter All stairs cut via stonecutter Locks stonecutter recipes matching the pattern.

docs.title: Category Prefixes & Specificity
docs.text:
By default, an unqualified pattern without a prefix (e.g. diamond_sword) matches across all workstations. You can restrict evaluation to specific crafting stations using category prefixes:

  • craft: / item:: Evaluates only standard 2x2 and 3x3 crafting workbench recipes.
  • potion: / brew:: Evaluates only Brewing Stand potion brewing actions.
  • enchant: / enchantment:: Evaluates only Anvil and Enchantment Table operations.
  • smelt: / furnace:: Evaluates Furnaces, Blast Furnaces, Smokers, and Campfires.
  • stonecut: / stonecutter:: Evaluates Stonecutter workstation recipes.

docs.title: Testing Gotcha: Operator Bypass (op-bypass)
docs.text:
In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

op-bypass: true

Are you testing with /op?

If your testing account has server operator status (/op), CraftingBlueprints will allow you to craft, brew, and enchant restricted recipes freely, bypassing all locks.

To properly test recipe restrictions as a normal player: 1. Temporarily deop yourself: /deop <your_player_name> 2. Alternatively, set op-bypass: false in config.yml and run /cb reload config.

To grant bypass rights to staff members or builders without giving them full operator status, assign the LuckPerms permission:

lp group moderator permission set craftingblueprints.bypass.ownership true

docs.title: Modular Preset Restriction Aggregation
docs.text:
When you install pre-built gameplay presets using /cb preset apply (e.g. Hardcore SMP or RPG Tiers), the plugin never modifies your config.yml.

Instead: 1. config.yml remains the sole authority for global operational mode (restrictions.mode: "restricted-only"). 2. Presets deploy their required restricted items to configs/presets/<preset_id>/restrictions.yml. 3. When the server boots or executes /cb reload, the engine performs a mathematical Set Union ($A \cup B$) between config.yml and all active preset restriction files. 4. When you uninstall a preset (/cb preset remove <preset_id>), its restrictions are cleanly purged from memory upon reload with zero leftovers.

docs.title: Recipe Auto-Scaffolder (/cb generate)
docs.text: Authoring dozens of blueprint YAML files by hand for existing crafting recipes can take hours. CraftingBlueprints includes a high-performance Recipe Auto-Scaffolder (/cb generate) that inspects your server's registered Bukkit recipes and external item plugins, automatically generating schema-valid blueprint YAML files with calibrated map aesthetics and scaled economy prices in seconds.

docs.title: Command Syntax & Parameters
docs.text:
/cb generate <source> [flags]

Permission Required: craftingblueprints.admin.generate (Default: op).

docs.title: Supported Recipe Sources (<source>)
docs.text:
The scaffolder can target specific categories, namespaces, or external plugins:

Source Identifier Source Scope & Content weapons Swords, axes, bows, crossbows, tridents, shields, and arrows. armor Helmets, chestplates, leggings, boots, horse armor, and turtle shells. tools Pickaxes, shovels, axes, hoes, shears, fishing rods, flint and steel, compasses, and brushes. potions All registered brewing PotionType variants. enchantments All registered vanilla enchantments. redstone Pistons, observers, hoppers, dispensers, droppers, repeaters, comparators, crafters, and TNT. food Craftable food items, golden carrots, and enchanted golden apples. building Stairs, slabs, walls, fences, gates, doors, bricks, terracotta, and concrete. all Every craftable recipe registered in Bukkit.recipeIterator() plus potions and enchantments. minecraft:<category> Scoped vanilla namespace filtering (e.g. minecraft:weapons). itemsadder Scans all custom items registered in the ItemsAdder registry (ia:<namespace:id>). oraxen Scans all custom items registered in the Oraxen registry (oraxen:<id>). nexo Scans all custom items registered in the Nexo registry (nexo:<id>).

docs.title: Scaffolder Flags Reference
docs.text: Flag Parameter Type Description --mode single | package Generates individual blueprints (single, default) or bundles items into packaged sets (package, chunked at $\le 24$ items per pack). --price-scale Decimal factor Multiplies base heuristic prices (Common: 250, Uncommon: 800, Rare: 2500, Legendary: 15000). Default: 1.0. --filter Regex pattern Selectively includes only recipes matching the regex (e.g. .*_sword$). --template Template ID Applies a reusable template mixin to all generated blueprints without hardcoding repeated fields. --out Relative path Destination file inside blueprints/ (e.g. --out weapons/swords.yml). Auto-appends .yml. --theme / --background Theme ID Sets the map background theme (forge, royal, technical_slate, dwarven_magma). --frame / --tier Frame ID / Tier Sets corner frame geometry (bracket, chamfer, diamond, runic, rosette, star). --prefix String Prefixes all generated blueprint IDs (e.g. --prefix smp_ generates smp_diamond_sword). --dry-run Flag Simulates generation and displays matched item counts without writing to disk or database. --force Flag Overwrites destination files and bypasses first-win ID collision warnings. --no-reload Flag Generates the YAML file on disk without immediately hot-reloading it into memory.

docs.title: 1. Scaffold All Swords into a Dedicated File
docs.text:
Scans all vanilla weapon recipes, filters for swords, applies a 1.5x price multiplier, and sets the dwarven forge map theme:

/cb generate minecraft:weapons --filter=".*_sword$" --price-scale=1.5 --theme=forge --frame=rosette --out="weapons/swords.yml"

docs.title: 2. Scaffold a Packaged Armor Set
docs.text:
Bundles all armor recipes into multi-item package portfolios:

/cb generate armor --mode=package --template=economy_tier_epic --out="armor/sets.yml"

docs.title: 3. Scaffold Custom Weapons from ItemsAdder
docs.text:
Scans custom weapons registered in ItemsAdder, preserving custom model data and names:

/cb generate itemsadder:weapons --price-scale=2.0 --out="custom/itemsadder_weapons.yml"

docs.title: Automatic Schema Header Injection
docs.text:
Every file generated by /cb generate automatically includes the relative language server schema directive at the top:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  diamond_sword:
    blueprint: DIAMOND_SWORD
    name: "<aqua>Diamond Sword Blueprint</aqua>"
    permanent: true
    price: 3750.0
    sell_price: 937.5
    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
    map:
      theme: technical_slate
      frame: bracket
      badge: crafting

This guarantees that as soon as you open the generated file in your code editor, full IntelliSense and schema validation are active immediately!

docs.title: Pre-Built Presets (/cb preset)
docs.text:
New server administrators frequently encounter the "blank-page problem": having to manually write dozens of YAML blueprints, permission groups, and recipe restrictions before seeing how the plugin transforms gameplay.

CraftingBlueprints solves this with a modular Preset Engine (/cb preset) that allows you to preview, deploy, customize, and cleanly uninstall balanced, production-ready progression packs with a single command.

docs.title: What is a Preset Package?
docs.text:
A Preset is a self-contained archive (.zip) or directory placed inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/presets/ with a modular structure:

plugins/CraftingBlueprints/presets/<preset_id>/
├── preset.yml             # Metadata manifest (id, name, author, version, description)
├── blueprints/            # Blueprint recipes (00_templates.yml, weapons.yml, armor.yml)
├── images/                # Visual map assets (backgrounds/, badges/, frames/)
└── config/                # Modular configuration files (groups.yml, restrictions.yml)

docs.title: The Inactive Repository vs Deployed Targets
docs.text:
• Inactive Repository (plugins/CraftingBlueprints/presets/): You can store, download, and organize preset .zip bundles or folders here without triggering live server imports or altering your database.
  • Active Deployment Targets: Presets only become active in-game when deployed via /cb preset apply <id> --confirm:
  • Blueprints deploy to: plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/presets/<id>/...
  • Images deploy to: plugins/CraftingBlueprints/images/presets/<id>/...
  • Configurations deploy to: plugins/CraftingBlueprints/configs/presets/<id>/...

docs.title: Built-In Modality Presets (PresetCatalog)
docs.text:
CraftingBlueprints ships with 4 built-in, production-balanced presets:

Preset ID Display Title Templates Blueprints Breakdown Progression & Gameplay Model hardcore_smp Hardcore SMP Survival 4 42 total (36 singles, 4 packages, 2 mysteries) restricted-only: Basic wood/stone free; iron unlocked via default group; Diamond, Netherite, Mending, and high-tier potions require blueprints with forge and royal map themes. rpg_tiers RPG Progression Tiers (T1–T5) 5 34 total (28 singles, 4 packages, 2 mysteries) restricted-only: T1 apprentice through T5 mythic weapons, armors, runes, and class kits unlocking via tiered blueprints (bracket $\rightarrow$ rosette). skyblock_coop Skyblock Co-op & Automation 4 28 total (22 singles, 4 packages, 2 mysteries) restricted-only: Island basics and farming free; diamond/netherite tools, beacons, shulker boxes, and silk touch require blueprints. prison_ranks OP Prison Ranks & Pickaxes 4 26 total (22 singles, 2 packages, 2 mysteries) restricted-only: Progressive ranks (default $\rightarrow$ rank_b $\rightarrow$ rank_c $\rightarrow$ rank_prestigious) unlock tiered drills, efficiency, and fortune pickaxes.

docs.title: 1. Listing Presets (/cb preset list)
docs.text:
Lists all built-in presets and local packages discovered in presets/:

/cb preset list

docs.title: 2. Previewing & Applying Presets (/cb preset apply)
docs.text:
Before modifying your live server, execute a dry-run preview:

/cb preset apply hardcore_smp --dry-run

The plugin analyzes the preset and displays the exact blueprint counts, target file paths, and collision checks without writing to disk or database.

To deploy the preset permanently, pass --confirm:

/cb preset apply hardcore_smp --confirm

docs.title: Dynamic Modifiers on Install:
docs.text:
You can scale prices, set usage limits, or isolate IDs during deployment:

# Multiply all prices by 1.5 (+50% cost)
/cb preset apply rpg_tiers --price-mult=1.5 --confirm

# Alternatively, use price increase percentage:
/cb preset apply rpg_tiers --price-increase=+25% --confirm

# Force all blueprints to have a finite 5-use craft limit:
/cb preset apply hardcore_smp --uses=5 --confirm

# Scale existing time durations by 2x:
/cb preset apply hardcore_smp --time-scale=2.0 --confirm

# Isolate under a custom prefix folder (prevents ID collisions):
/cb preset apply rpg_tiers --prefix="season2" --confirm

# Filter to selectively import only swords and armor:
/cb preset apply hardcore_smp --filter=".*(sword|armor).*" --confirm

docs.title: 3. Clean Uninstallation (/cb preset remove <id>)
docs.text:
Administrators can completely uninstall an active preset without leaving leftover residues (zero-leftovers):

/cb preset remove hardcore_smp

This command: 1. Safely deletes deployed folders across blueprints/presets/hardcore_smp/, images/presets/hardcore_smp/, and configs/presets/hardcore_smp/. 2. Clears image caches and reloads groups and recipe restrictions. 3. Automatically prunes the recipes from the database and broadcasts a sync signal to all worker nodes.

docs.title: 4. Exporting Custom Blueprints (/cb preset export)
docs.text:
To bundle existing blueprints into a shareable preset package:

/cb preset export my_custom_pack --zip

Creates a distributable my_custom_pack.zip archive inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/presets/ containing your blueprint YAMLs, images, and config files.

docs.title: Zero config.yml Mutation Rule
docs.text:
Deploying or removing presets NEVER modifies your config.yml.

  • Why? Directly appending or deleting lines from config.yml often corrupts custom comments, destroys formatting, and creates merge conflicts in Git.
  • The Solution: Presets deploy modular configuration files to configs/presets/<id>/groups.yml and configs/presets/<id>/restrictions.yml. The plugin's engine aggregates these modular files in memory dynamically at runtime.

docs.title: Master / Worker Safety Guard
docs.text: In multi-server MySQL networks: * Preset modifications (apply, remove, export) are strictly restricted to the Primary Management Node (sync-from-files: true). * Executing /cb preset apply on a Worker Node (sync-from-files: false) is blocked immediately with a clear localized error redirecting you to execute the command on the master server.

docs.title: Multi-Server Synchronization (MySQL / MariaDB)
docs.text:
If you operate a BungeeCord or Velocity network where players switch between different game servers (e.g. Lobby, Survival, Skyblock, Factions), you can connect CraftingBlueprints to a central MySQL or MariaDB database.

This guarantees that when a player unlocks a blueprint on one server, their recipe knowledge, remaining craft counts, and active expiration timers synchronize instantly across every server on the network.

docs.title: 2. The Golden Rule of Multi-Server Networks
docs.text:
The Golden Rule: One Primary Node Only

To prevent database divergence, split-brain conflicts, and race conditions, you must designate strictly ONE Primary Management Node on your entire network (typically your Hub, Lobby, or Staff server).

All other sub-servers (Survival, Skyblock, Factions, Prison) must operate as Worker Nodes.

docs.title: Configuration Comparison:
docs.text:
Primary Management Node (Hub / Admin)Worker Nodes (Survival, Skyblock, etc.) 

file-management:
  # ENABLED ONLY ON THIS SERVER:
  sync-from-files: true
  prune-deleted: true
  auto-reload:
    enabled: true
* This primary server reads your local YAML blueprints in blueprints/ and synchronizes them into the shared MySQL database. * Whenever you edit files or run /cb reload, the primary node writes changes to the database and dispatches a network signal ping (cb_sync_signals).

file-management:
  # STRICTLY FALSE ON ALL GAME SERVERS:
  sync-from-files: false
  prune-deleted: false
  auto-reload:
    enabled: false
* Worker nodes load all registered blueprints directly from the shared MySQL database into memory. * They never overwrite the database with local files, ensuring 100% data consistency. * They automatically detect database signal pings from the primary node and refresh their memory cache in real time with zero manual commands.

docs.title: 3. Database Credentials Configuration
docs.text:
Configure the database connection block in plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml on every server:

# Set storage backend to mysql
database-type: mysql

# Shared database parameters
database-name: crafting_blueprints
database-host: 127.0.0.1
database-port: 3306
database-user: cb_user
database-password: "your_secure_password"

docs.title: MariaDB / MySQL Privilege Setup (SQL)
docs.text:
Run these queries on your database server to provision the user and database cleanly:

CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS crafting_blueprints CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS 'cb_user'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'your_secure_password';

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP, INDEX, ALTER, LOCK TABLES 
ON crafting_blueprints.* TO 'cb_user'@'%';

FLUSH PRIVILEGES;

docs.title: 4. Real-Time Heartbeat Signal Ping (cb_sync_signals)
docs.text:
In traditional plugins, updating configurations on a multi-server network requires running /reload on every single sub-server. CraftingBlueprints eliminates this operational friction:

  1. Master Reload: An administrator edits a blueprint YAML file on the primary node and runs /cb reload blueprints (or lets the auto-reloader detect the file save).
  2. Signal Dispatch: The master node writes the updated blueprints to MySQL and emits an atomic reload signal into the cb_sync_signals table.
  3. Automatic Worker Invalidation: During their background heartbeat cycle (every 3 to 5 seconds), all worker nodes detect the new signal timestamp, invalidate their local blueprint caches, and reload the updated definitions from MySQL.
  4. Outcome: All sub-servers update within seconds without a single console command or server restart.

docs.title: 5. Cross-Server Map Virtualization & PDC Relinking
docs.text:
In cross-server networks, Minecraft map IDs frequently clash: * Map ID 104 on the Survival server might be a Diamond Sword blueprint. * Map ID 104 on the Lobby server might be the server spawn hub map.

CraftingBlueprints solves this using PDC Visual Key Virtualization: * The physical map item stores the normalized visual_key in its PersistentDataContainer (cb_map:single:diamond_sword:...). * When a player switches from Survival to Lobby via Bungee/Velocity, the MapRelinkListener intercepts the item upon player join or inventory open. * It queries the local server's BlueprintMapRegistry and re-links the item's MapView to the local canonical Map ID in-place. * Guaranteed Outcome: The physical map always renders the correct blueprint graphic on the local server without ever overwriting or corrupting world maps on that server.

docs.title: 6. Player Lifecycle & Quick-Relog Protection
docs.text: When players switch rapidly between servers (e.g. clicking a portal or executing /server survival): * WaitingManager and cb_reservations prevent race conditions where Server B attempts to load player data before Server A has finished flushing recent crafts to MySQL. * If a player rejoins within milliseconds, active memory state is preserved with atomic monitor locks, eliminating lost updates and rollback glitches.

docs.title: Standalone Server Storage (SQLite)
docs.text: By default, CraftingBlueprints uses an embedded SQLite relational database engine. This is the optimal configuration for standalone Survival servers, Skyblock worlds, RPG realms, and minigames operating on a single server instance.

docs.title: Zero-Configuration Setup
docs.text:
SQLite requires zero external software, no database servers, and no user management. CraftingBlueprints automatically provisions the database file and manages schema migrations on startup.

In plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml:

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Database Storage Configuration
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Storage engine backend: sqlite
database-type: sqlite

# Database filename (saved as crafting_blueprints.db)
database-name: crafting_blueprints

docs.title: File Location & Data Schema
docs.text:
All persistent data is stored directly in a single file inside your plugin directory:

your-server/
└── plugins/
    └── CraftingBlueprints/
        └── crafting_blueprints.db

This database maintains: * cb_player_data: All unlocked blueprints, remaining craft usage counts, and expiration timestamps per player UUID. * ITEM_BLUEPRINTS: Blueprints created in-game via GUI or commands (is_file_managed: false). * cb_schema_version: Automated schema migration version markers.

docs.title: Performance & Concurrency Architecture
docs.text:
• Zero Main-Thread Blocking: All database read and write operations execute on asynchronous background daemon worker threads. Player crafting, inventory clicks, and server ticks are never blocked waiting for disk I/O.
  • Keyed FIFO Task Dispatcher: Writes for each player are strictly queued in First-In-First-Out order, guaranteeing atomic check-and-consume invariants even during high-frequency crafting events.
  • Capacity: Embedded SQLite handles single-server workloads effortlessly, supporting over 150+ concurrent active players with sub-millisecond local query latencies.

docs.title: Live Backup & Restore Procedures
docs.text: Because CraftingBlueprints uses asynchronous transactions, you can safely back up your database while the server is live:

docs.title: Creating a Backup
docs.text:
1. Navigate to plugins/CraftingBlueprints/.
  2. Copy crafting_blueprints.db to your backup directory or cloud storage.
  3. You can safely run this copy operation from a scheduled backup script while players are online.

docs.title: Restoring from Backup
docs.text:
1. Stop the server safely: 
    /stop
  2. Replace plugins/CraftingBlueprints/crafting_blueprints.db with your backup copy.
  3. Start the server. The plugin validates the database integrity upon boot and resumes operations immediately.

docs.title: Tutorial: Distributing Blueprints via Crates & Quests
docs.text: Blueprints make fantastic high-value rewards for loot crates, battle passes, dungeon boss drops, and questlines. Because CraftingBlueprints guarantees Physical Overflow Preservation, players will never lose blueprint items even if their inventories are completely full when completing a quest or opening a crate.

docs.title: 1. The Core Console Reward Command
docs.text:
Whenever a third-party plugin executes a console command to reward an online player, execute:

cb give %player% <blueprint_id> [amount]

Physical Preservation Guarantee

If the recipient's inventory happens to be 100% full when a crate opens or a quest finishes, CraftingBlueprints automatically drops the leftover blueprint items safely onto the ground directly at the player's feet (world.dropItem(...)). No items ever vanish into thin air.

docs.title: Tutorial: 3-Use Magic Forge Scrolls for RPG Servers
docs.text:
In MMORPG, fantasy, and dungeon servers, legendary equipment should feel rare and earned. Giving players permanent access to endgame weapons can quickly flood the player market and break economic tiers.

This tutorial guides you through creating a Limited-Use Magic Forge Scroll that allows an adventurer to craft a legendary weapon exactly 3 times before the scroll's magic dissolves and the recipe locks again.

docs.title: Step 1: Restrict the Target Weapon
docs.text:
Open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml and ensure your target weapon is restricted:

restrictions:
  mode: "restricted-only"
  restricted-items:
    - "netherite_sword"

docs.title: Step 2: Configure the 3-Use Magic Scroll
docs.text:
Create a new file named rpg_forge_scrolls.yml inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  astral_blade_scroll:
    # Target item to unlock
    blueprint: NETHERITE_SWORD
    name: "<gradient:#9900EE:#00FFFF><bold>Scroll of the Astral Blade</bold></gradient>"

    # Durability Model: 3 crafts only; no temporal timer
    permanent: false
    time: 0
    uses: 3

    # Physical item: Enchanted Ancient Parchment
    item:
      material: PAPER
      custom_model_data: 2005
      glowing: true

    # Visual map aesthetic if inspected in catalog
    map:
      theme: void_grimoire      # Deep obsidian violet arcane grimoire
      frame: runic              # Gothic runic apex corner architecture
      badge: smithing           # Workstation plaque
      icon_scale: 2
      drop_shadow: true
      stamp:
        show: true
        style: wax_seal
        text: "3x"
        border_color: "#a855f7"

    # Lore card with dynamic uses placeholder
    lore:
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>---------------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<gray>Artifact Type:</gray> <light_purple>Arcane Forge Scroll</light_purple>"
      - "<gray>Remaining Forges:</gray> <yellow><bold>{uses} / 3 crafts</bold></yellow>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>---------------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<yellow>Allows a master smith to forge the Astral</yellow>"
      - "<yellow>Blade up to 3 times before dissolving.</yellow>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>---------------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<dark_gray>Right-click in hand to bind this knowledge.</dark_gray>"

Hot-reload the blueprints: 

/cb reload blueprints

docs.title: Step 3: Grant the Scroll & Test Progression
1. Granting the Scroll via Command:
docs.text: /cb give Steve astral_blade_scroll 1

docs.title: 2. Binding the Knowledge:
docs.text: The player places the scroll into their main hand and Right-Clicks. A sound effect plays, and the player unlocks 3 crafting uses.

docs.title: 3. First Craft (Counter: 3 $\rightarrow$ 2):
docs.text:
The player crafts their first sword. Chat and action bar notify the player: 

[CraftingBlueprints] Recipe crafted! Remaining uses: 2

docs.title: 4. Shift-Click Bulk Crafting Test:
docs.text:
• If the player places materials for 5 swords into the crafting matrix and Shift-Clicks:
  • The engine evaluates: $\min(\text{MatrixCrafts: 5}, \; \text{InventorySpace: 36}, \; \text{RemainingUses: 2}) = \mathbf{2}$.
  • Exactly 2 swords are crafted into their inventory.
  • Remaining uses decrement from 2 to 0.
  • The recipe immediately locks, and the remaining materials for 3 swords remain safely untouched inside the crafting table!

docs.title: Tutorial: Gating Netherite Gear Behind Bastion Loot in SMP
docs.text:
In vanilla Minecraft, dedicated players often rush Netherite armor and tools within the first 48 hours of a server launch, trivializing PvE encounters and crashing survival economies.

This step-by-step cookbook tutorial shows you how to configure CraftingBlueprints to gate all Netherite equipment behind rare, physical blueprint maps that can only be found in Nether Bastion Remnant loot chests.

docs.title: Step 1: Enable Whitelist Mode in config.yml
docs.text:
Open plugins/CraftingBlueprints/config.yml and ensure your server is running in Selective Whitelist Mode with Netherite equipment restricted:

# ------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Recipe Restrictions & Whitelist Mode
# ------------------------------------------------------------ #

restrictions:
  # In 'restricted-only' mode, all basic wood, stone, iron, and diamond
  # recipes remain completely free and natural for all players!
  mode: "restricted-only"

  # ONLY items matching this list will require an unlocked blueprint:
  restricted-items:
    - "netherite_sword"
    - "netherite_pickaxe"
    - "netherite_axe"
    - "netherite_shovel"
    - "netherite_hoe"
    - "netherite_helmet"
    - "netherite_chestplate"
    - "netherite_leggings"
    - "netherite_boots"

Save the file and execute: 

/cb reload config

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Ancient Netherite Blueprint
docs.text:
Create a new file named netherite_progression.yml inside plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  ancient_netherite_smithing:
    # Target item unlocked in 3-slot Smithing Table
    blueprint: NETHERITE_CHESTPLATE
    name: "<gradient:#FF5555:#FFAA00><bold>Ancient Netherite Smithing Technique</bold></gradient>"

    # Permanent unlock: once learned, the player can upgrade Netherite indefinitely
    permanent: true
    time: 0
    uses: 0

    # In-game physical item
    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    # Map visual schematic
    map:
      theme: dwarven_magma       # Molten volcanic basalt background
      frame: rosette             # Regal Guilloché corner rosettes
      badge: smithing            # Workstation icon on top-left
      icon_scale: 2
      drop_shadow: true
      item_outline:
        enabled: true
        width: 2
        color: "gold"

    # Lore card
    lore:
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>---------------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<gray>Classification:</gray> <gold><bold>Ancient Smithing Knowledge</bold></gold>"
      - "<gray>Rarity Tier:</gray> <light_purple>MYTHIC</light_purple>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>---------------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<yellow>Grants the forbidden technique required</yellow>"
      - "<yellow>to forge Netherite gear in a Smithing Table.</yellow>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>---------------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<dark_gray>Hold this map and Right-Click to memorize.</dark_gray>"

Reload the blueprints to activate the new schematic: 

/cb reload blueprints

docs.title: Step 3: Add to Bastion Chest Loot Tables
docs.text: You can distribute this blueprint to players via vanilla datapack loot tables or popular loot plugins.

docs.title: Option A: Via MythicDrops or CustomLoot Plugin
docs.text:
Configure the console reward command in your loot table configuration:

commands:
  - "cb give %player% ancient_netherite_smithing 1"

docs.title: Option B: Vanilla Datapack Loot Table Injection
docs.text:
In your server datapack (e.g. data/minecraft/loot_tables/chests/bastion_treasure.json):

{
  "type": "minecraft:item",
  "name": "minecraft:filled_map",
  "weight": 15,
  "functions": [
    {
      "function": "minecraft:set_nbt",
      "tag": "{PublicBukkitValues:{\"craftingblueprints:id\":\"ancient_netherite_smithing\"}}"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Step 4: Verification & Testing in Survival
docs.text:
1. Test Failure as Unauthorized Player:
  2. Temporarily deop yourself: /deop <your_player_name>
  3. Place a Diamond Chestplate, a Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template, and a Netherite Ingot into a Smithing Table.
  4. The output slot remains locked! Clicking the result warns that you lack the required blueprint.
  5. Grant & Memorize:
  6. Grant yourself the blueprint map: /cb give <your_player_name> ancient_netherite_smithing 1
  7. Hold the high-resolution map in hand and Right-Click. A chime sound plays and chat confirms you have memorized the recipe.
  8. Test Successful Forging:
  9. Return to the Smithing Table. The Netherite Chestplate is now unlocked and crafts successfully!

docs.title: Tutorial: Setting Up a Blueprint Economy Shop (Vault)
docs.text: CraftingBlueprints integrates directly with Vault and your server's economy provider (EssentialsX, Economy, etc.), allowing players to purchase and sell blueprints using server currency directly from the interactive /cb item list catalog GUI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Ensure the following plugins are installed on your server:

  1. CraftingBlueprints
  2. Vault
  3. Any Vault-compatible economy plugin (e.g. EssentialsX Economy, TheEconomy)

docs.title: Step 1: Configure Reusable Economy Templates
docs.text:
To maintain consistent pricing across your server, create an economy template file at plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/00_economy_tiers.yml:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
templates:
  # Tier 1: Apprentice Gear
  economy_apprentice:
    price: 1500.0
    sell_price: 375.0
    extra:
      tier: "APPRENTICE"

  # Tier 2: Journeyman Equipment
  economy_journeyman:
    price: 7500.0
    sell_price: 1875.0
    extra:
      tier: "JOURNEYMAN"

  # Tier 3: Master Artifacts
  economy_master:
    price: 35000.0
    sell_price: 8750.0
    extra:
      tier: "MASTER"

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Blueprint Shop Items
docs.text:
Create your blueprint definitions referencing the economy templates (e.g. plugins/CraftingBlueprints/blueprints/industrial_tools.yml):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=./blueprint.schema.json
singles:
  diamond_drill_blueprint:
    blueprint: DIAMOND_PICKAXE
    name: "<gradient:#00AAFF:#00FFAA><bold>Industrial Diamond Drill Blueprint</bold></gradient>"
    permanent: true

    # Inherit Master tier economy ($35,000 buy / $8,750 sell)
    templates:
      - economy_master

    item:
      material: FILLED_MAP
      glowing: true

    map:
      theme: technical_slate
      frame: bracket
      badge: crafting

    lore:
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>-----------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<gray>Target Equipment:</gray> <white>{target_item}</white>"
      - "<gray>Tier Classification:</gray> <gold><bold>{tier}</bold></gold>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>-----------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<yellow>Catalog Buy Price:</yellow> <green>${price}</green>"
      - "<yellow>Catalog Sell Value:</yellow> <gold>${sell_price}</gold>"
      - "<dark_gray><strikethrough>-----------------------------</strikethrough></dark_gray>"
      - "<dark_gray>Left-Click in catalog to purchase with Vault.</dark_gray>"

Reload the blueprints to update the catalog: 

/cb reload blueprints

docs.title: Step 3: The In-Game Purchasing Flow
docs.text:
1. The player opens the server catalog: 
    /cb item list
  2. The player browses through the pages. Blueprints with a configured price: display their cost and a locked indicator.
  3. The player Left-Clicks the Industrial Diamond Drill Blueprint:
  4. A confirmation menu opens displaying the $35,000 purchase price and the player's current balance.
  5. Upon clicking Confirm Purchase:
  6. Vault checks the player's account balance.
  7. If funds are sufficient, Vault deducts $35,000.
  8. The blueprint is unlocked immediately on the player's account.
  9. A chime sound plays, and the status icon switches to Unlocked!

docs.title: Step 4: Selling Blueprints Back to the Catalog
docs.text: If a player has an unlearned physical blueprint item in their inventory that defines a sell_price:: * Players can run /cb sell (or click the sell icon in the catalog GUI) to surrender the physical item and receive the configured refund value ($8,750) deposited into their Vault economy balance.
